features.title: Phase 0: Foundations & Infrastructure — Feature Spec

assumptions: **Market Focus**: Primary focus for check management is the Egyptian market.
**Storage**: Supabase Storage will be used for all files.
**Auth**: User is already authenticated (from Phase 0).
**Currency**: Default currency is EGP, but system supports others as defined in Phase 0.
edgeCases: **Offline Access**: What happens if the user tries to upload a document while offline? (System should notify user and retry when online).
**Plan Limits**: How does the system handle a free user trying to add a 3rd unit? (System MUST enforce the 2-unit limit and show upgrade prompt).
**Duplicate Checks**: How does the system handle entering the same check number twice? (System should warn the user about potential duplicates).
functionalRequirements: **FR-001**: System MUST allow users to Create, Read, Update, and Delete (CRUD) Portfolios.
**FR-002**: System MUST allow users to CRUD Property Units with attributes: type, area, status, finishing level, address, and price.
**FR-003**: System MUST support multi-tab unit details: Overview (specs), Payments (installments), and Documents (files).
**FR-004**: System MUST provide secure document storage for units using signed URLs for privacy.
**FR-005**: System MUST automatically generate an installment schedule based on total price, down payment, start date, and frequency.
**FR-006**: System MUST allow manual logging of payments against generated installments.
**FR-007**: System MUST track check-specific metadata: check number, bank name, cash date, and photo.
**FR-008**: System MUST support RTL (Arabic) and LTR (English) layouts for all screens in Phase 1A.
features.title: Feature Specification: Mobile - Portfolio & Units (Phase 1A)
userStories: *Why this priority**: Core functionality that builds the foundation for tracking any assets. Without units, no other features (payments, documents) can function.
*Independent Test**: User can create a portfolio, add a unit to it with full details (type, area, price), and view the unit in the portfolio list.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: Essential for record-keeping and fulfilling the "manager" role of the application.
*Independent Test**: User can navigate to a unit's detail screen, switch between Overview and Documents tabs, and successfully upload/view a PDF contract.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: Critical for financial management, which is a key value proposition of the app.
*Independent Test**: User can define a total price and installment frequency, see a generated plan, and mark one installment as "Paid".
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: High value for the primary target market (Egypt), where checks are a standard real estate payment method.
*Independent Test**: User can add a check number and bank name to a payment record and see the check's status in a dedicated check list.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:

assumptions: React will be upgraded from 18.2.0 to React 19 as part of this task (atomic upgrade with Next.js 16.2).
The `apps/web` package (Phase 2, not yet bootstrapped) is out of scope for this upgrade.
The mobile app (`apps/mobile`, Expo/React Native) is not affected by a Next.js version change.
The existing shadcn/ui components, next-intl, and @supabase/ssr packages have versions compatible with Next.js 16.2 (or compatible upgrades are included in this work).
The `eslint-config-next` version will be updated to match the new Next.js version.
`next-browser` is an experimental tool; its output format may change in future releases.
CI/CD (Vercel deployment) supports Next.js 16.2 without configuration changes.
edgeCases: What happens when Next.js 16.2 introduces a breaking change in a dependency (e.g., shadcn/ui, next-intl, or @supabase/ssr)?
How does the upgrade behave if the lock file from the old dev server is stale after an unexpected process kill?
What happens when `next-browser` is run without an active dev server?
How does browser log forwarding interact with CI environments where no browser is attached?
functionalRequirements: **FR-001**: The admin app MUST be upgraded to Next.js 16.2 in a single direct pass from 14.2.3, using official Next.js codemods to resolve breaking changes, and all existing features MUST remain intact.
**FR-002**: The admin app MUST build and pass type-checking with zero errors after the upgrade.

**FR-003**: The dev configuration MUST explicitly set browser log forwarding to "warnings and errors" (overriding the Next.js 16.2 default of "errors only"), so AI coding agents receive React 19 deprecation warnings alongside errors in the terminal.

**FR-004**: An `AGENTS.md` MUST be created at the project root AND the existing `apps/admin/AGENTS.md` MUST be updated — both MUST include the official Next.js 16.2 `<!-- BEGIN:nextjs-agent-rules -->` section directing agents to read locally bundled docs in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/`.

**FR-005**: A `CLAUDE.md` MUST be created at the project root (with `@AGENTS.md` directive) AND the existing `apps/admin/CLAUDE.md` MUST be confirmed to reference `@AGENTS.md`, so Claude Code automatically loads agent rules at both the monorepo root and admin-app level.
**FR-006**: The `@vercel/next-browser` skill MUST be installed and accessible via the `/next-browser` command in Claude Code.

**FR-007**: React MUST be upgraded to React 19 (and react-dom to 19) atomically as part of this task, along with all peer dependency version conflicts introduced by the combined Next.js 16.2 + React 19 upgrade.
**FR-008**: The dev server lock file behavior MUST be verified — starting a second `next dev` process in the same directory MUST produce the structured error with PID and URL.
features.title: Feature Specification: Upgrade Next.js to 16.2 with AI Developer Skills
userStories: *Why this priority**: The upgrade is foundational — all AI developer features in 16.2 depend on running this version. Staying on 14.x means missing security patches and future compatibility as Supabase, shadcn/ui, and other dependencies evolve.

*Independent Test**: Run the admin app and confirm all existing pages (login, dashboard, portfolio list, unit detail, installment tracker, document viewer) load and function correctly after the upgrade.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:

*Why this priority**: AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor) work primarily through the terminal. Without browser log forwarding, client-side errors are invisible to agents, slowing down debugging. This feature directly improves AI-assisted development velocity.
*Independent Test**: Can be tested by introducing a deliberate client-side error, running `pnpm dev`, and confirming the error appears in the terminal output without opening a browser devtools panel.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:

*Why this priority**: Research shows agents using bundled docs achieve 100% task accuracy vs 79% using skill-based retrieval. The admin app already has a placeholder AGENTS.md; it needs to be updated to the official 16.2 format.
*Independent Test**: Open AGENTS.md in the project root and in `apps/admin/`. Confirm the `<!-- BEGIN:nextjs-agent-rules -->` section is present with the correct directive.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: This is an experimental, additive capability. It enhances agent debugging but does not block any existing workflows. It should be set up after the core upgrade is stable.

*Independent Test**: Run `npx skills add vercel-labs/next-browser`, then type `/next-browser` in Claude Code with the dev server running. Confirm the skill responds with component tree or screenshot output.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:

assumptions: **CNG + prebuild workflow**: The `android/` directory exists in `apps/mobile/`, so the project uses the prebuild workflow — `npx expo prebuild --clean` is required to regenerate the native project.
**`ios/` directory absent**: Only `android/` was observed in the directory listing; if an `ios/` directory exists, CocoaPods must also be re-run (`cd ios && pod install --repo-update`).

**NativeWind v5 required**: Expo SDK 55 with React 19 is incompatible with NativeWind v4's babel transform approach. The migration to NativeWind v5 (`react-native-css` based) is a required part of this upgrade, not optional.
**No audio/video features yet**: The app does not currently use `expo-av` (not listed in `package.json`), so the `expo-av` → `expo-audio`/`expo-video` migration is out of scope.

**React Compiler opt-in deferred**: Enabling the React Compiler (`"experiments": { "reactCompiler": true }`) is out of scope for this upgrade. It may be evaluated in a follow-up once the SDK 55 upgrade is stable.
**Hermes v1 deferred**: The opt-in to Hermes v1 (`useHermesV1: true` in `expo-build-properties`) will be evaluated after the upgrade is stable.

**Dark mode deferred**: NativeWind v5 drops `darkMode: "class"` and uses CSS `light-dark()` / `@media (prefers-color-scheme)`. An in-app manual dark mode toggle requires custom override logic not yet stable in NativeWind v5 preview. Dark mode support will be added in a follow-up spec once NativeWind v5 stable ships. This upgrade removes the `darkMode: "class"` config and delivers light mode only.
**No `sdkVersion` field**: `app.json` does not currently have an explicit `sdkVersion` field, which is the correct SDK 55+ practice — no change needed.
edgeCases: **NativeWind class not found**: If a Tailwind class used in the app does not exist in Tailwind CSS v4's default theme, the component renders without that style. Developer must audit all custom utility classes against the new v4 config format.

**`android/` directory exists (prebuild workflow)**: Since native directories exist, `npx expo prebuild --clean` must be run after dependency bumps to regenerate the native projects for SDK 55's React Native version.
**Monorepo Metro config**: The existing `metro.config.js` has monorepo-specific `watchFolders` and `nodeModulesPaths` settings — these must be preserved during any Metro config format changes.
**expo-router version jump**: Upgrading from `expo-router ~3.5` to v4 (SDK 55 default) may include file-based routing API changes. All existing routes must be verified to still resolve correctly.
**`@hookform/resolvers` in devDependencies**: This is currently in `devDependencies` but is used in production code — it should be moved to `dependencies`.
functionalRequirements: **FR-001**: System MUST upgrade `expo` to `~55.0.0` and run `npx expo install --fix` to align all Expo-managed packages to their SDK 55 compatible versions.
**FR-002**: System MUST upgrade `react` to `^19.0.0` and `react-native` to the version mandated by Expo SDK 55.
**FR-003**: System MUST upgrade `@types/react` to `^19.0.0` to match the React 19 runtime.
**FR-004**: System MUST add `react-native-worklets-core` as a dependency (required by `react-native-reanimated` since SDK 54).
**FR-005**: System MUST remove `newArchEnabled: true` from `app.json` (New Architecture is the default in SDK 55 and the field is no longer needed).
**FR-006**: System MUST remove `@babel/core` from `devDependencies` (implicit Expo dependency).
**FR-007**: System MUST remove `expo-constants` from explicit `dependencies` (implicit Expo dependency — still available, just not declared).

**FR-008**: System MUST migrate NativeWind from v4 to v5 (pinned to exact version `nativewind@5.0.0-preview.2` — no semver range — to prevent uncontrolled bumps to potentially more broken preview iterations) and Tailwind CSS from v3 to v4, updating `babel.config.js`, `metro.config.js`, `tailwind.config.js`, and `nativewind-env.d.ts` accordingly.

**FR-008a**: System MUST migrate ALL existing components in `apps/mobile/` and `packages/ui/src/` that use `className` props to the `useCssElement` wrapper pattern — no screen or component may be left with an unstyled bare RN component using `className`. Migration is complete only when every screen renders with correct styles verified in the manual regression walkthrough (SC-005).
**FR-009**: System MUST fix all React 19 breaking changes in custom components: remove `forwardRef` wrappers (pass `ref` as a regular prop), update `Context.Provider` → `Context` where applicable.
**FR-010**: System MUST run `npx expo prebuild --clean` to regenerate the `android/` native project for the new React Native version.
**FR-011**: System MUST verify `expo-doctor` exits with zero errors/warnings after all changes.
**FR-012**: System MUST verify `pnpm --filter mobile typecheck` exits with zero errors after all changes.
**FR-013**: System MUST move `@hookform/resolvers` from `devDependencies` to `dependencies` (it is a production runtime dependency).
features.title: Feature Specification: Upgrade Expo SDK to v55
userStories: *Why this priority**: The SDK version is the foundation of every other upgrade task. Nothing else can proceed until the build is green on SDK 55.
*Independent Test**: Running `npx expo-doctor` from `apps/mobile/` exits with zero warnings and zero errors after the upgrade. The app starts without crashes on both iOS and Android simulators.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: React 19 introduces breaking changes that affect component patterns used throughout the codebase. These must be fixed before the app is usable.

*Independent Test**: Every screen in the app renders without console errors or warnings related to deprecated React APIs. The unit list, unit detail, auth flows, and onboarding wizard all render and function correctly.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: SDK 55 with React 19 requires NativeWind v5 (the current v4 babel transform is incompatible). This is the largest single migration task in the upgrade.

*Independent Test**: Every screen that uses Tailwind class names renders correctly in both AR (RTL) and EN (LTR) modes. The design tokens (colors, spacing, typography) are visually identical to the pre-upgrade build.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: Cleanup tasks are not blocking but prevent technical debt and future upgrade friction.
*Independent Test**: Running `npx expo-doctor` and `pnpm --filter mobile lint` both exit with zero issues after cleanup is applied.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:

assumptions: Supabase Postgres remains the managed database host. The database schema (tables, views, RPC functions, triggers including `enforce_unit_limit`) is unchanged.
Postgres Row-Level Security policies are removed; multi-tenancy and data isolation are enforced exclusively by Laravel authorization policies at the application layer (resolved from Q1).
The Laravel API owns the user identity store. Users are created fresh; there are no existing production user records to carry over since the backend has not been launched (resolved from Q2 & Q3).
Laravel 13.x (latest stable) is the target version for `apps/api/`.
Laravel Sanctum handles API token issuance. Laravel Socialite handles Google and Apple OAuth callbacks.
Phone OTP is delivered via an SMS gateway (e.g., Twilio or Vonage) integrated into the Laravel auth layer.
Push notifications continue to use the Expo Push Notification service. The Laravel scheduler calls the Expo Push API directly in place of the former Supabase Edge Function.
Document storage uses Laravel's storage driver pointed at an S3-compatible bucket (replacing Supabase Storage). Signed URLs are generated by the storage driver.
TypeScript types for API contracts are generated from the Laravel OpenAPI spec and replace `packages/types/supabase.ts`.
The `supabase` CLI remains available only for Postgres migration management (`supabase db push`). Supabase Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, and Realtime are not used.
edgeCases: What happens when the API is unreachable from the mobile app? → App shows a connectivity error state; no crash.
What happens when a scheduled job fails partway through (e.g., push service unavailable)? → Failed notifications must be retried; partial runs must be idempotent.
What happens when a user's account is deleted mid-session? → Subsequent API calls with their token return 401; all tokens are revoked as part of the deletion cascade.
What happens to portfolio data shared with other members when the owner deletes their account? → The entire portfolio and all its data are deleted; member access is revoked simultaneously.
functionalRequirements: *Authentication**
**FR-001**: The API MUST implement phone OTP authentication: 6-digit codes, 5-minute expiry, with dedicated strict per-user and per-IP rate limits on OTP request and verification endpoints.
**FR-002**: The API MUST support Google and Apple as OAuth sign-in providers via the standard provider callback flow.

**FR-003**: The API MUST issue access tokens with 1-hour expiry and refresh tokens with 30-day expiry. Logout MUST revoke only the token presented in the current request; tokens on other devices remain valid. A separate "sign out of all devices" action MUST revoke all tokens for the authenticated user.
**FR-004**: The API MUST maintain its own user identity table as the authoritative user store.
*Data Access**
**FR-005**: The API MUST expose versioned REST endpoints (e.g., `/api/v1/`) for all data entities: portfolios, units, installments, post-dated checks, documents, and rental records.
**FR-006**: Financial summary endpoints (ROI, portfolio summary, cash flow) MUST source all figures from the existing Postgres views and RPC functions. No financial logic in application code.
**FR-007**: The API MUST enforce multi-tenant data isolation: every data endpoint scopes its query to the authenticated user's owned and shared (via `portfolio_members`) records.

**FR-007a**: The `portfolio_members` join table MUST support configurable per-member roles. Defined roles: `viewer` (read-only access to portfolio data) and `editor` (full read/write access to portfolio and unit data, excluding membership management). Only the portfolio owner can add, remove, or change member roles.
**FR-008**: The API MUST enforce subscription plan limits at the application layer (unit count, portfolio count, team seats, Excel exports) and return a `plan_limit_exceeded` error when exceeded.
*Background Jobs**
**FR-009**: The scheduler MUST run four recurring jobs: daily-reminders (06:00), check-risk-scan (07:00), weekly-delay-digest (Sunday 08:00), fx-rates-sync (00:00).
**FR-010**: All scheduled jobs MUST be idempotent — re-running them for the same window must not send duplicate notifications.
*Storage**
**FR-011**: Document uploads MUST be stored in private storage. Retrieval MUST use signed URLs with a maximum 1-hour expiry.
*Admin**
**FR-012**: All admin-tier operations MUST write an entry to `audit_logs` (actor, action, target, before/after snapshot) before the operation completes.
**FR-013**: Admin endpoints MUST be protected by an admin-role check independent of regular user authorization.
*Client Integration**
**FR-014**: The mobile app repository layer (`features/*/repository/`) MUST call the Laravel REST API in place of all direct supabase-js calls.
**FR-015**: The admin web data-fetching layer MUST call the Laravel REST API in place of all Supabase SSR client calls; the `@supabase/ssr` dependency is removed.
**FR-016**: TypeScript API types MUST be generated from the Laravel API's OpenAPI contract and replace `packages/types/supabase.ts`.
*Authorization Model (replaces Postgres RLS)**

**FR-017**: All data queries MUST be scoped at the application layer via authorization policies — the API service-level DB connection is the only DB identity. Postgres RLS policies are removed. Multi-tenancy is enforced entirely by the application.
**FR-018**: A positive authorization test (authorized user can access) and a negative test (unauthorized user is blocked) MUST exist for every endpoint before the endpoint is marked done.
*Rate Limiting**

**FR-024**: A global per-user rate limit MUST apply to every API endpoint. Authenticated requests exceeding the limit MUST receive a `rate_limit_exceeded` response with a `Retry-After` header. Auth endpoints (OTP request, OTP verify, token refresh) retain their own stricter per-user and per-IP limits independent of the global limit.
*Observability**
**FR-020**: The API MUST integrate Sentry for server-side exception tracking. All unhandled exceptions and job failures MUST be captured and source-mapped to a Sentry release.
**FR-021**: Scheduled job failures MUST be captured as Sentry errors with enough context (job name, affected record IDs) to diagnose without reading raw logs.
*Account Deletion**

**FR-022**: The API MUST provide an account deletion endpoint that permanently and immediately removes all user data: profile, portfolios, units, installments, checks, documents, rental records, tokens, and push tokens. No data is retained after deletion.
**FR-023**: Account deletion MUST be irreversible. The API MUST require explicit confirmation (e.g., a re-authentication step or confirmation token) before executing the deletion.
*Error Responses**
**FR-019**: The API MUST return structured JSON error responses with machine-readable codes: `plan_limit_exceeded`, `unauthorized`, `not_found`, `validation_error`, `rate_limit_exceeded`.
features.title: Feature Specification: Backend in Laravel
userStories: *Why this priority**: Authentication is the entry gate to every other feature. Nothing else can be built, tested, or demonstrated without a working auth layer.

*Independent Test**: Achievable by completing a full phone OTP registration, a Google sign-in, and an Apple sign-in on the mobile app, verifying that tokens are issued and that a subsequent API call succeeds with each token.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: Managing real estate data is the core product. This is the primary deliverable for Phase 1.

*Independent Test**: Achievable by creating a portfolio with one unit, adding an installment, and verifying that the portfolio ROI figure returned by the API matches the Postgres `calculate_unit_roi` function output.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: Timely reminders are a key product promise. Missed or late notifications erode investor trust immediately.
*Independent Test**: Achievable by triggering each job manually via an artisan command and verifying that push notifications are dispatched and the `currency_rates` table is updated.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: Document privacy is a legal and trust requirement.
*Independent Test**: Achievable by uploading a document, waiting for the signed URL to expire, and confirming the URL returns 403 or 404 after expiry.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: Admin operations support investor onboarding and resolution of support cases but are not blocking for the investor-facing product.
*Independent Test**: Achievable by overriding a user's subscription tier from the admin panel and confirming an `audit_logs` entry is written and the user's plan limit changes immediately.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:

assumptions: The Laravel API already has (or will have, within this feature's scope) endpoints covering all operations currently handled directly by the Supabase client: OTP send/verify, social OAuth callback, profile upsert, portfolio insert, unit insert, and session validation.
Supabase continues to be used as the managed Postgres host; this feature only removes the Supabase SDK from frontend clients — the database itself is not migrated.

The `packages/types/src/supabase.ts` file is only referenced by internal tooling (type generation scripts) and not imported by any frontend runtime code; if it is imported at runtime, those imports must also be removed.
Existing users will be migrated or asked to re-authenticate when the new release is deployed; a one-time migration script or a "re-login" prompt is acceptable.
The feature targets the current codebase state: the Supabase SDK is used in 13 identified files across mobile and admin apps (see scope below).
RTL/LTR display, dark/light mode, and i18n behaviour are unaffected by this change; only data and auth layers change.
edgeCases: What happens when the Laravel API is unreachable during authentication? The app shows a network error and allows the user to retry.
What happens to users who have an active Supabase session at the time of release? Their session is invalidated; they are prompted to log in again via Laravel.
What happens if environment variables for Supabase still exist in `.env` files after the SDK is removed? They should be deleted to avoid confusion; the build must succeed without them.
What happens to TypeScript types that were auto-generated from the Supabase schema? They are either deleted (if unused by frontend) or replaced with types generated from the Laravel OpenAPI contract.
functionalRequirements: **FR-001**: The mobile app MUST NOT import or reference any `@supabase/*` package at runtime.
**FR-002**: The admin panel MUST NOT import or reference any `@supabase/*` package at runtime.
**FR-003**: The mobile app MUST authenticate users (OTP, Google, Apple) exclusively through the Laravel API.
**FR-004**: The admin panel MUST authenticate users (email/password) exclusively through the Laravel API.
**FR-005**: Session tokens issued by Laravel MUST be stored and retrieved using the existing local storage mechanism on mobile (AsyncStorage) and cookies on the web.
**FR-006**: All data operations currently using `supabase.from(table).select/insert/update/upsert()` in the mobile app MUST be replaced with calls to the corresponding Laravel REST endpoints.
**FR-007**: The auth state listener (`supabase.auth.onAuthStateChange`) in the mobile app MUST be replaced with equivalent logic driven by the Laravel session/token lifecycle.

**FR-008**: The `packages/types/src/supabase.ts` auto-generated file MUST either be deleted or clearly marked as unused and excluded from frontend builds; frontend types MUST come from the Laravel OpenAPI contract.

**FR-009**: All Supabase-specific environment variables (`EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`) MUST be removed from all `.env` files used by the frontend apps.
**FR-010**: The `@supabase/supabase-js` dependency MUST be removed from `apps/mobile/package.json`.
**FR-011**: The `@supabase/supabase-js` and `@supabase/ssr` dependencies MUST be removed from `apps/admin/package.json`.
**FR-012**: After removal, both apps MUST build successfully with zero Supabase-related import errors.

**FR-013**: The Laravel API MUST expose all endpoints needed to replace the removed Supabase calls (OTP send/verify, OAuth callback, profile upsert, portfolio create, unit create, session validation).
features.title: Feature Specification: Remove Supabase from Frontend Clients
userStories: *Why this priority**: Phone OTP is the primary entry point for the app. If authentication breaks, no other feature is usable.
*Independent Test**: Run the mobile app, trigger the phone-OTP flow end-to-end; verify the user reaches the authenticated home screen and a valid session token is stored locally.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: Social sign-in is the second primary login path and shares the same authentication gate as OTP.
*Independent Test**: Trigger Google and Apple sign-in flows in the mobile app; confirm successful session creation backed by Laravel.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: Onboarding is the first post-login experience; data must persist reliably to unblock all subsequent features.
*Independent Test**: Complete all three onboarding screens with a fresh account; verify records exist in the database via the Laravel API.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: Admin operations are critical for product management, but the admin panel has fewer users than the mobile app.
*Independent Test**: Log into the admin panel with a valid admin account; verify the dashboard loads with data fetched exclusively from the Laravel API.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: Session persistence is foundational; breaking it forces all users to re-login after every restart.
*Independent Test**: Close and reopen the mobile app or reload the admin panel; confirm the user remains authenticated without re-entering credentials.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:

assumptions: **Existing Database Host**: The underlying database host will be migrated to a generic Postgres provider.
**Auth Flow**: We assume the current OTP and Social Auth flows implemented in the backend are sufficient replacements for the external service.
**Storage Config**: The backend will be configured with S3-compatible storage to handle files.
edgeCases: **Session Migration**: What happens to users currently logged in via the external auth service? They will likely be forced to re-log.
**Data Persistence**: Ensuring that existing data in the database instance remains accessible or is migrated if the host changes.
**Large File Transfers**: Handling timeouts or failures when moving storage from external buckets to the new storage provider.
functionalRequirements: **FR-001**: System MUST remove all proprietary external service client dependencies from all packages and apps.
**FR-002**: Mobile and Admin apps MUST use the primary API client for all authentication and data operations.
**FR-003**: Proprietary external service configuration and migration directories MUST be removed from the repository.
**FR-004**: Database schema management MUST be moved entirely to the native backend migration system.
**FR-005**: All environment variables related to the external proprietary service MUST be removed or replaced with generic backend variables.
**FR-006**: Storage operations MUST be refactored to use the backend's storage abstraction.
**FR-007**: System MUST support migrating the database to a generic Postgres host (e.g., AWS RDS, DigitalOcean).
**FR-008**: System MUST support using S3-compatible storage for all file management operations.
features.title: Feature Specification: Remove Supabase Backend
userStories: *Why this priority**: Authentication is the gatekeeper of the app. Removing external service dependencies for auth is the most critical step in decoupling.

*Independent Test**: Can be tested by performing a login flow in Mobile/Admin and verifying that the request goes to the application backend and returns an authentication token, and no calls are made to the external service.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: High. File storage is a key feature used in onboarding and unit management.
*Independent Test**: Upload an image in the Mobile app and verify it is stored via the backend's storage system and retrieved via a backend-generated URL.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: Medium. Important for workflow consistency and removing the last "backend" footprint of the external service.
*Independent Test**: Running native backend migration status commands should show all tables as migrated, and external migration directories can be deleted without losing schema info.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:

assumptions: This specification covers the **local development environment** only; production deployment uses managed cloud services (object storage, managed cache, managed database)
The local database service replaces the Supabase-managed Postgres instance removed in spec 006
Developers are expected to have a container runtime (Docker Desktop or equivalent) installed before running the stack
The mobile app (Expo) and admin web panel (Next.js) run on the host machine in development — they are not containerized
The API backend (Laravel), database, cache, storage, queue worker, and mail capture are the services that must be containerized
Default port assignments are configurable via environment variables to avoid conflicts with other local services
The S3-compatible storage service is used for local development only; production uses a cloud-hosted object storage service
A `.env.example` file will document all required environment variables; developers copy it to `.env` before first run
Existing Laravel Horizon configuration is used as-is for queue worker behavior
edgeCases: What happens when a service fails to start because a required port is already in use on the developer's machine?
How does the application behave when the cache service becomes temporarily unavailable while the database and API are still running?
What happens to queued jobs that are mid-processing when the queue worker service is stopped?
How are credentials and secrets distributed to developers without being committed to source control?
What happens when two developers run the stack simultaneously on the same network (port conflicts, shared volumes)?
functionalRequirements: **FR-001**: The entire application service stack MUST be startable with a single command from the repository root
**FR-002**: Each service MUST be independently startable and stoppable without affecting other running services
**FR-003**: The file storage service MUST implement the S3 API (bucket creation, object upload/download, presigned URL generation, bucket access policies)
**FR-004**: The cache service MUST support key-value caching, queue list operations, and pub/sub messaging as required by the application
**FR-005**: The database service MUST be compatible with Postgres 15 and accept standard database connection strings
**FR-006**: All data stored in any service (files, database records, cache data) MUST persist across service restarts
**FR-007**: All services MUST expose ports to the host machine to enable direct connection from debugging tools and GUI clients
**FR-008**: All credentials, hostnames, and port assignments MUST be configurable via environment variable files — no secrets hardcoded in service definitions
**FR-009**: A queue worker service MUST run alongside the API service to consume and process background jobs
**FR-010**: A mail capture service MUST intercept all outbound emails from the application and make them viewable via a local web interface
**FR-011**: Each service MUST define health checks so that dependent services only start after their dependencies are confirmed healthy
**FR-012**: All service definitions MUST be version-controlled in the repository alongside application code
**FR-013**: The service definitions MUST include separate configuration profiles for development and CI/test environments
features.title: Feature Specification: Docker Infrastructure Setup
userStories: *Why this priority**: This is the foundation for every other story. Without a running local stack, no development, testing, or debugging is possible for any team member.

*Independent Test**: Run the startup command on a clean machine that has only a container runtime installed; verify all services are accessible and the API can connect to the database, storage, and cache within 2 minutes.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:

*Why this priority**: File storage is a core product feature. Property documents, rental agreements, and scanned checks must be uploadable, retrievable via signed URLs, and organized by bucket. Development requires a local equivalent that mirrors production behavior.
*Independent Test**: Upload a file through the API, retrieve it via a generated signed URL, then verify the URL expires after the configured window and the file is no longer accessible.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:

*Why this priority**: Scheduled jobs and caching are central to the OAR B feature set. They depend on a live cache/queue service. This is secondary to getting core CRUD and storage working (P1 stories).

*Independent Test**: Dispatch a background job (e.g., daily-reminders) manually and verify the queue worker picks it up and processes it; separately, prime a cache entry and verify subsequent requests are served from cache.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:

*Why this priority**: Supabase backend was removed in spec 006. A local database replaces it and is foundational, but is lower priority than the API + storage story since it was the last piece to be extracted.
*Independent Test**: Run all application migrations against the local database from scratch; seed the database with test data; verify the API returns correct responses using that data.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:

*Why this priority**: Email delivery is used for OTP authentication and scheduled notifications but is not blocking for core CRUD or storage development. A local mail capture service enables safe testing without risk of sending to real recipients.
*Independent Test**: Trigger an OTP dispatch through the API and verify the email appears in the local mail inbox with correct content within seconds.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:

assumptions: The queue worker (Horizon) is explicitly excluded from the containerized stack; it may be added as an opt-in override or run manually when needed
Jobs dispatched to the queue are silently enqueued without error; they will be processed whenever a worker is started
This specification covers the local development environment only; production uses managed cloud services
The local database replaces the Supabase-managed Postgres instance removed in spec 006
Developers are expected to have a container runtime (Docker Desktop or equivalent) installed
The admin web panel (Next.js) and mobile app (Expo) continue to run on the host machine, not in containers
Redis is included for caching only — queue processing is excluded from this stack profile
A `.env.example` file documents all required environment variables; developers copy it to `.env` before first run
The containerized stack has 5 services: `postgres`, `redis`, `minio`, `minio-init` (one-shot), `mailpit`, and `app`
edgeCases: What happens when a service fails to start due to a port conflict on the developer's machine?
How does the application behave when the cache service becomes temporarily unavailable?
What happens to jobs dispatched to the queue when no worker is running (are they silently enqueued or do they cause errors)?
How are credentials and secrets distributed to developers without committing them to source control?
functionalRequirements: **FR-001**: The application service stack (excluding the queue worker) MUST be startable with a single command from the repository root
**FR-002**: Each service MUST be independently startable and stoppable without affecting other running services
**FR-003**: The file storage service MUST be S3-API-compatible (bucket creation, object upload/download, presigned URL generation, private access policies)
**FR-004**: The cache service MUST support key-value caching operations required by the application
**FR-005**: The database service MUST be compatible with Postgres 15 and accept standard database connection strings
**FR-006**: All data stored in any service (files, database records, cache) MUST persist across service restarts
**FR-007**: All services MUST expose ports to the host machine for direct connection from GUI tools and debugging utilities
**FR-008**: All credentials, ports, and hostnames MUST be configurable via environment variable files — no secrets hardcoded in service definitions
**FR-009**: A mail capture service MUST intercept all outbound emails and present them in a local web interface
**FR-010**: Service health checks MUST be defined so dependent services only start after their dependencies are confirmed healthy
**FR-011**: All service definitions MUST be version-controlled in the repository alongside application code
**FR-012**: The queue worker service is explicitly **out of scope** — it MUST NOT be included in the default startup command
**FR-013**: Background jobs MUST remain dispatchable by the application without errors even when no queue worker is running (jobs queue silently)
features.title: Feature Specification: Docker Infrastructure (No Queue Worker)
userStories: *Why this priority**: The containerized stack is the starting point for all development. Removing the queue worker reduces the resource footprint and simplifies the startup sequence for developers who are not actively working on background-job features.

*Independent Test**: Run the startup command on a clean machine with only a container runtime installed; verify all services are accessible and the API connects to the database, cache, and file storage within 2 minutes.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: File storage is a core product feature. Developers must be able to test document upload and signed URL retrieval flows locally without cloud access.
*Independent Test**: Upload a file through the API, retrieve it via a signed URL, then verify the URL expires after the configured window.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:

*Why this priority**: Caching is important for correctness testing — verifying that stale cache is invalidated on mutation. Queue processing is excluded from this spec; Redis is used for caching only.
*Independent Test**: Prime a cache entry via the API; verify subsequent requests are served from cache; trigger a mutation and verify the cache entry is invalidated.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: The local database replaces the previously managed Supabase instance. It is foundational but lower priority than storage, which has more complex local-development requirements.
*Independent Test**: Run all migrations from scratch against the local database; seed test data; verify API responses reflect the seeded data correctly.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:

*Why this priority**: Background job development is an occasional need; the queue worker is excluded from the always-on stack to save resources. Manual execution provides a lightweight alternative for testing job logic.
*Independent Test**: Trigger a job command manually from the API container and verify it completes successfully and produces the expected side effects.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: Email delivery is used for OTP authentication and notifications but is not blocking for core development work.
*Independent Test**: Trigger an OTP dispatch; verify the email appears in the local mail inbox within seconds with correct content.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:

assumptions: The Laravel API is fully deployed and accessible at the configured base URL for each environment (local, staging, production); this feature covers client integration only, not API server setup.

The OpenAPI specification exported from the Laravel API accurately reflects all endpoints consumed by both clients; any undocumented endpoint used by the UI is a defect in the API spec, not a permitted workaround.
Both apps share the same user identity system — an investor who registers on mobile can log into the admin panel with the same credentials if they have admin privileges.
Biometric authentication on mobile (PIN/Face ID unlock) is out of scope for this feature; this feature covers network-layer API authentication only.
Offline-first sync with conflict resolution (Phase 1.5 per the product plan) is out of scope; this feature delivers online-first data access with graceful degradation.
The admin panel runs in a browser environment where cookies and secure storage are available; the mobile app runs on iOS and Android where secure keychain storage is available.
edgeCases: What happens when the API returns a 401 mid-session on the admin panel after a long idle period?
How does the mobile app behave when the device has no connectivity at launch (no cached data)?
What happens when the API returns partial data (e.g., a portfolio list but missing financial summaries)?
How are concurrent mutations handled when two admin users edit the same investor record simultaneously?
functionalRequirements: **FR-001**: Both the mobile app and admin panel MUST authenticate users exclusively through the Laravel API using token-based sessions; no direct database access is permitted from the client.
**FR-002**: The mobile app MUST automatically refresh authentication sessions transparently when the access token nears expiry, without interrupting the investor's current activity.
**FR-003**: The admin panel MUST redirect unauthenticated users to the login page for any route that requires authentication.
**FR-004**: All data displayed in both clients (portfolios, units, installments, checks, documents, rental income, financial summaries) MUST be sourced exclusively from the Laravel API.
**FR-005**: Every API request MUST be sent with properly typed request and response shapes; untyped or loosely typed API calls are forbidden.
**FR-006**: After any data mutation (create, update, delete), both clients MUST refresh the affected data views without requiring the user to manually reload.
**FR-007**: The mobile app MUST display data from the most recent successful API fetch when the API is temporarily unreachable (stale-while-revalidate behavior).

**FR-008**: Both clients MUST display localized error messages (Arabic or English based on user preference) for all API error conditions — including authentication failures, validation errors, plan limit errors, and network failures.
**FR-009**: The system MUST surface a subscription upgrade prompt — not a generic error — when the API returns a plan limit exceeded response.
**FR-010**: API response types MUST be generated from the Laravel API's OpenAPI contract and committed to the shared types package; no hand-authored API types are permitted.
**FR-011**: All network requests MUST include appropriate timeout and retry handling; a failed request MUST NOT leave the UI in a permanently loading state.
**FR-012**: Authentication tokens MUST NOT be stored in plaintext in any log, analytics event, or client-side state that persists beyond the session.
features.title: Feature Specification: Laravel API Client Integration
userStories: *Why this priority**: Authentication is the gateway to every feature. Without a working, secure login flow connected to the Laravel backend, no other mobile functionality is accessible.

*Independent Test**: The mobile app login screen can be tested end-to-end by entering valid credentials and verifying that the portfolio list screen appears with real data loaded from the API. Invalid credentials must show an Arabic-language error message without crashing the app.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: The admin panel is the operations backbone. Without a functional API connection, staff cannot manage investor accounts or respond to support requests.

*Independent Test**: The admin panel login page can be tested in isolation by logging in and verifying that the investor list loads from the API. Any single management action (e.g., viewing an investor's portfolio) must successfully retrieve and display live API data.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: The "Auto-ROI" promise is a core product differentiator. Stale financial figures undermine investor trust.

*Independent Test**: Record a new installment payment on mobile and verify that the portfolio summary card refreshes on the same screen showing the updated ROI figure, without the investor manually pulling to refresh.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: Resilience directly affects perceived quality. An app that crashes or shows JSON error blobs on any network issue loses investor confidence quickly.

*Independent Test**: Disable the API server and open the mobile app. The portfolio list must display either cached data or a clear "couldn't load" message in the user's language — no unhandled exceptions, no blank screens.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:

assumptions: Docker Desktop (or Docker Engine + Compose plugin) is the only required tool on the developer's host machine.
The monorepo structure is retained — apps remain under `apps/` and shared packages under `packages/`, but dependency installation is handled per-container rather than at the root workspace level.

The Expo mobile app is run via the Expo CLI dev server inside a container or locally with the API URL pointed at the Docker host; it does not itself need to be containerized for device testing (physical devices cannot connect to a container's localhost).
npm workspaces will be used to replace pnpm workspaces; the workspace configuration moves from `pnpm-workspace.yaml` to the `workspaces` field in the root `package.json`.
Existing database schemas and migrations are not affected by this change — only the tooling and containerization layer changes.
The current Docker infrastructure from spec `007-docker-infrastructure` and `008-docker-no-queue` serves as the starting baseline for this migration.
edgeCases: What happens when Docker is not installed or the Docker daemon is not running? The developer should see a clear error message from Docker itself rather than a cryptic failure.
How does the system handle port conflicts if a developer already has a local service running on the same ports?
What happens if a developer has leftover pnpm lockfiles or node_modules from before the migration? The project should work correctly regardless.
How does the Expo app behave when the Docker API is unreachable (e.g., containers stopped)? It should show a connection error, not crash silently.
functionalRequirements: **FR-001**: The project MUST be startable using only Docker Compose, with no host-level package manager installation required.
**FR-002**: All package management scripts, documentation, and CI references MUST use npm and npx exclusively — pnpm and turbo MUST be removed from the project.
**FR-003**: Each application (mobile, admin web, API) MUST have its own dedicated Dockerfile that builds and runs it in isolation.
**FR-004**: The Docker Compose configuration MUST define all required services (API, admin, database, cache) with correct networking so services can communicate by container name.
**FR-005**: The Expo React Native mobile app MUST read its API base URL from an environment variable that is set differently per environment (local Docker, staging, production).
**FR-006**: The mobile app environment variable for the API URL MUST be injectable at build/start time without requiring source code changes.
**FR-007**: All existing npm workspace packages (types, schemas, ui, i18n, utils) MUST continue to resolve correctly when built inside their respective app containers.
**FR-008**: The project MUST NOT contain any references to pnpm-specific files (`pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `.npmrc` with pnpm config) after migration.
**FR-009**: Developer documentation (README or quickstart) MUST be updated to reflect the Docker-first workflow with npm.
features.title: Feature Specification: Docker-First Project with NPM
userStories: *Why this priority**: This is the primary developer experience goal. Every other story depends on containers being up and running. It unblocks all contributors immediately.
*Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by running `docker compose up` on a freshly cloned repo on a machine with only Docker installed, and verifying all services respond on their expected ports.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: Without this, mobile developers cannot test against the real backend while using Docker for the API layer, breaking the development workflow for the mobile team.
*Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by starting the Docker services, then launching the Expo app, and confirming network requests from the app reach the containerized API (visible in API logs).
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: Reduces resource consumption and startup time for focused development. Valuable once the base setup (P1) is stable.
*Independent Test**: Can be tested by starting only the API container and running API tests against it, verifying the API functions independently.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:

assumptions: The admin panel serves internal staff only; there is no public-facing registration route.

All seven sections (Dashboard, Portfolios, Units, Installments, Checks, Documents, Users) are stubs — they render placeholder content acknowledging the section name, not full feature implementations. Full content per section is handled by later feature specs.
The existing middleware auth logic (cookie-based token check) is retained as-is; only the routing layer is modified, not the authentication mechanism.

The shared admin shell layout (sidebar + header) is a new component created as part of this spec. Navigation items for all seven sections are hardcoded initially (i18n keys, not dynamic from API). Sections without implemented content (Portfolios, Units, Installments, Checks, Documents, Users) appear in the sidebar as visually disabled / "coming soon" items.
All section pages except Dashboard currently have no data-fetching; their implementations are left to dedicated feature specs.
RTL/LTR switching is achieved via the existing `dir` attribute on the `<html>` element in the locale layout — no additional CSS framework changes required.
edgeCases: How does the app behave when the API is unreachable during initial dashboard load? A visible error state should appear, not a blank page or spinner stuck indefinitely.
What happens when the admin panel runs under a sub-path (e.g., behind a reverse proxy at `/admin`)? Routes should remain functional.
What happens if a user manually types an unsupported locale in the URL (e.g., `/fr/dashboard`)? The middleware should fall back to the default locale.
functionalRequirements: **FR-001**: The root path (`/`) MUST redirect to the default locale login page (`/ar/login`) for unauthenticated users.
**FR-002**: Visiting `/{locale}` when authenticated MUST redirect to or render the admin dashboard — never the Next.js boilerplate template.

**FR-003**: The admin panel MUST define a protected route group that requires authentication; all pages within this group MUST redirect unauthenticated users to `/{locale}/login`. A single admin role is used — all authenticated users have access to all seven sections; route-level RBAC is out of scope for this spec.

**FR-004**: The admin panel MUST define routes for the following sections, each as a distinct stub page: Dashboard (overview), Portfolios, Units, Installments, Checks, Documents, Users (investor/tenant accounts — not admin staff accounts).

**FR-005**: Each section page MUST render within a shared admin shell layout (sidebar navigation + header), not as a standalone full-page without navigation. Sidebar navigation MUST display all seven section items; sections without full implementations MUST be shown as visually disabled with a "coming soon" indicator rather than being hidden.
**FR-006**: A 404 not-found page MUST be shown when an admin navigates to an undefined route within the `/{locale}/` namespace.
**FR-007**: All page-level text content MUST be loaded from i18n translation files — no hardcoded strings in route pages.
**FR-008**: The locale segment MUST control the page language and text direction for all routes (Arabic → RTL, English → LTR).
**FR-009**: The middleware MUST preserve the originally requested URL as a post-login redirect parameter so the admin lands on their intended page after authentication.
features.title: Feature Specification: Fix Admin Next.js Routes
userStories: *Why this priority**: The current home page shows a Next.js boilerplate template ("To get started, edit the page.tsx file"). No admin work can be done until the routing resolves to a real, usable starting point. Every other admin feature depends on this baseline navigation working.

*Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by visiting `http://localhost:3000`, confirming the redirect to the login page, logging in, and verifying the browser URL resolves to the dashboard section showing real admin UI content (not the Next.js template).
*Acceptance Scenarios**:

*Why this priority**: Without distinct navigable routes for each section, the admin panel cannot scale beyond a single-page app. Each section needs its own URL to support bookmarking, deep-linking, and browser history.
*Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by visiting each section URL directly in the browser and confirming each renders its own page content without redirecting back to the dashboard.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: Localization is a core requirement of OAR B. If protected routes break locale behavior, Arabic admins cannot use the panel effectively.
*Independent Test**: Can be tested by navigating to `/{locale}/portfolios` in both `ar` and `en` locales and confirming both pages render with the correct language and text direction.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:

assumptions: Existing test files (`OtpAuthTest.php`, `TokenTest.php`, `PortfolioTest.php`, `DocumentTest.php`, `Authorization/PortfolioPolicyTest.php`, `Admin/AdminAuthorizationTest.php`, and others) may already cover some scenarios; the task is to audit and complete coverage, not necessarily replace existing tests.
The test database is separate from the development database and is reset between test runs using Laravel's `RefreshDatabase` trait.
S3/MinIO file storage is faked in tests using Laravel's `Storage::fake()` to avoid external dependencies.
OAuth (Social login) endpoints are tested with mocked OAuth provider responses, not real provider calls.
The Pest testing framework (already in use in the project) is the target framework; no migration to another tool is required.
Phone numbers in OTP tests use the E.164 format (e.g., `+201234567890`).
All currency codes in tests use valid ISO 4217 3-letter codes (e.g., `EGP`, `USD`).
edgeCases: What happens when a resource ID that exists belongs to another tenant? The response must be 404 (not 403) to prevent ID enumeration.
What happens when a currency code is 2 or 4 characters long (not exactly 3)? A 422 validation error must be returned.
What happens when an OTP code is submitted for a different phone number than it was issued for? A 422 response must be returned.
What happens when a rental's `end_date` is the same day as `start_date`? Validation must reject this.
What happens when a `DELETE /account` is called and the user has active subscriptions? The account deletion must still succeed (or be explicitly blocked — behavior must be defined and tested).
functionalRequirements: **FR-001**: The test suite MUST cover every route defined in `routes/api.php`, with at least one happy-path test and one failure-path test per endpoint.
**FR-002**: Every endpoint that requires authentication MUST have a test asserting a 401 response when called without a token.
**FR-003**: Every resource endpoint MUST have a cross-tenant isolation test asserting that user A cannot access user B's data (expecting 404, not 403).
**FR-004**: Every endpoint that enforces plan limits MUST have a test asserting the 403 plan-limit response when the limit is exceeded.
**FR-005**: Every endpoint with validation rules MUST have tests for invalid and missing required fields, asserting 422 responses with field-specific error details.
**FR-006**: Admin-protected endpoints MUST have a test asserting a 403 response when called by a non-admin authenticated user.
**FR-007**: The OTP rate-limit endpoint MUST have a test asserting a 429 response after the threshold is exceeded.
**FR-008**: Document upload tests MUST use a storage mock or fake driver so no real S3/MinIO calls are made during test runs.
**FR-009**: All tests MUST use database transactions or explicit rollback so each test run starts from a clean state.
**FR-010**: The test suite MUST be runnable in CI with a single command and produce a clear pass/fail result.
**FR-011**: Tests for endpoints returning paginated results MUST verify the pagination structure (current page, per-page count, total).
**FR-012**: Token refresh MUST be tested to verify the old refresh token is revoked after use.
features.title: Feature Specification: Complete Laravel API Test Suite
userStories: *Why this priority**: Authentication is the gateway to all other endpoints. A silent regression here can lock out all users or silently grant unauthorized access.
*Independent Test**: Run the auth test suite in isolation; all auth endpoints can be exercised against a seeded in-memory or test database with no other feature dependencies.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: Data isolation between tenants is a core security invariant. Unverified authorization allows data leakage between investor accounts.
*Independent Test**: Seed two distinct users, each with their own portfolios/units, and verify cross-user access is denied for every resource endpoint.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: Portfolios and units are the primary domain objects; most other resources depend on them.
*Independent Test**: Seed one user with one portfolio and one unit; all CRUD tests for these two resources can run independently with that fixture.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: Financial data accuracy is a core product promise; incorrect status or amount data directly impacts investor decisions.
*Independent Test**: Seed one user, one portfolio, one unit; create installments, checks, and rentals under that unit. All sub-resource tests run with that fixture.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: Documents often contain sensitive legal files; leaking signed URLs or allowing unauthorized deletion are security risks.
*Independent Test**: Seed one user with one unit; mock the S3 storage client so tests do not depend on real object storage.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: Admin actions have elevated impact (subscription changes, broadcast messages); untested admin paths can introduce critical bugs or security gaps.
*Independent Test**: Seed one admin user and several investor users; admin tests run with that fixture independently.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: These are simpler endpoints but account deletion is irreversible and needs special validation.
*Independent Test**: Seed one user; all profile endpoint tests are self-contained.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:

features.title: Spec 013 — Remaining Backend API Gaps
userStories: *Acceptance criteria:**
`POST /api/v1/units/{unit}/valuations` stores a manual valuation record.
`GET /api/v1/units/{unit}/valuations` returns the valuation history.
`POST /api/v1/units/{unit}/images` uploads a unit photo.
`DELETE /api/v1/units/{unit}/images/{id}` removes a unit image.

assumptions: This feature is backend-focused; mobile and admin UI changes are limited to consuming existing or documented API behavior and are not part of the core scope.
Existing document and unit-image upload flows remain the first storage lifecycle targets; future file categories should reuse the same storage behavior.
Local object storage is required for development and verification; production may use any S3-compatible managed storage provider.
Required local buckets are `documents` and `images`, both private by default.
Payment work focuses on a reusable provider contract and normalized outcomes, not a full checkout user interface.
Existing providers and webhooks remain supported while the shared gateway contract is introduced.
Provider credentials and object storage credentials are supplied through environment configuration maintained outside committed secrets.
Existing authentication, authorization, subscription, invoice, and audit-log concepts remain in force.
edgeCases: A valid file upload is interrupted before the complete object is stored.
A user requests a signed access link for a deleted or expired file record.
A stored object exists but its metadata record is missing, or metadata exists but the object is missing.
The local storage console port or object storage API port is already in use.
A payment provider sends the same webhook more than once or sends events out of order.
A payment event references a subscription, user, invoice, or plan that no longer exists.
A payment provider returns success after the client has abandoned the payment flow.
A provider credential is missing, expired, or configured for the wrong environment.
functionalRequirements: **FR-001**: The API MUST own all user file upload, retrieval-link generation, metadata recording, and deletion flows for documents and images.
**FR-002**: Stored user files MUST be private by default and accessible only through API-authorized, time-limited access links.

**FR-003**: The API MUST validate file size, file type, ownership, and target resource before accepting an upload. Allowed types: **PDF, DOCX, XLSX, CSV** for documents; **JPG, PNG, WEBP** for images — enforced via both MIME type and file extension (dual check to prevent extension spoofing).
**FR-004**: The system MUST record file metadata including owner, target resource, category, original filename, stored path, MIME type, size, and creation time.
**FR-005**: Deleting a user file through the API MUST remove both the user-visible metadata and the underlying stored object, or report a clear partial-failure state for operator follow-up.

**FR-005a**: When a file upload succeeds but metadata persistence fails, the system MUST perform a best-effort deletion of the stored object as part of rollback and MUST log a warning if that cleanup deletion also fails; no user-visible file record may remain.
**FR-006**: The local development environment MUST provide S3-compatible object storage with documented API and console access.
**FR-007**: Local object storage startup MUST create the required private buckets automatically and preserve objects across service restarts.
**FR-008**: The API MUST be configurable to use local object storage in development and cloud-compatible object storage in deployed environments without changing client behavior.

**FR-009**: The system MUST define a shared payment gateway **interface** (contract) covering: provider identification, configuration readiness check, payment-session initiation, inbound event verification, event normalization to a common result, and provider-specific error mapping. Each payment provider (Stripe, Paymob, RevenueCat, future providers) supplies its own independent implementation of this interface; no concrete provider implementation is required in this feature — only the interface and the integration harness that consumes it.
**FR-010**: Payment event handling MUST update subscription and invoice outcomes through a single normalized flow, regardless of provider.

**FR-011**: Payment event processing MUST be idempotent: the system stores the provider's own event/webhook ID on each invoice and rejects any incoming event whose provider event ID already exists, preventing duplicate invoices and conflicting subscription transitions.
**FR-012**: The system MUST reject unverifiable or unauthorized payment provider events before any subscription or invoice changes occur.
**FR-013**: Provider-specific secrets, credentials, and environment selectors MUST be configurable outside committed source and must never be returned in API responses or logs.

**FR-014**: Storage and payment failures MUST produce user-safe error responses and structured log events containing: event type, resource ID, provider name (if applicable), error class, and timestamp. Raw file paths, credentials, and raw provider payloads MUST NOT appear in logs or API responses.

**FR-015**: Automated checks MUST cover successful storage lifecycle, unauthorized storage access, local object storage connectivity, payment provider success events, invalid provider events, duplicate events, and provider misconfiguration.
features.title: Feature Specification: S3 Storage and Payment Gateway Integration
userStories: *Why this priority**: File storage is required for property deeds, contracts, checks, images, and future evidence attachments. Without a complete API-managed storage lifecycle, users cannot trust uploaded documents or safely view them later.

*Independent Test**: Upload an allowed document and image through the API, retrieve each through a time-limited access link, confirm unauthorized users cannot access them, delete them, and verify the stored objects are removed.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: Local development and automated verification need a predictable storage service. Developers should be able to start the stack and immediately exercise real storage behavior.

*Independent Test**: Start the local stack from a clean checkout, verify storage health, confirm required private buckets exist, upload a file through the API, and verify the object appears in the local storage console.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:

*Why this priority**: Subscription payment behavior already spans multiple providers. A consistent provider contract reduces duplicate logic, keeps webhook handling auditable, and makes future providers easier to add.

*Independent Test**: Add a provider implementation using only the documented gateway contract, process a successful test payment event, and verify subscription and invoice outcomes match existing providers.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: Storage and payments are trust-sensitive flows. When they fail, users and support need clear status without exposing secrets or sensitive provider payloads.

*Independent Test**: Simulate unavailable storage, invalid file data, invalid payment signatures, and provider timeouts; verify the API returns safe errors, records diagnostic events, and leaves user data in a consistent state.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:

assumptions: The admin panel already has an authenticated shell (login works); this feature only adds the navigable section pages inside that shell.
All 9 sections listed in FR-001 represent the full set of planned admin areas; no additional sections are in scope for this placeholder phase.
Section-level access control uses role-based permissions already defined in the backend; this feature only enforces visibility and route protection, not defining the roles themselves.
Light and dark mode are in scope at the layout level (inherited from the existing admin shell); placeholder page content should not hard-code colors.
Mobile responsiveness for the admin panel is out of scope for this feature; the admin panel targets desktop-first users.
Icons for each sidebar section will use a standard icon library already integrated into the admin panel; icon selection is an implementation detail.
edgeCases: What happens when an admin tries to navigate to a section URL that does not exist in the placeholder set? A proper 404 page is shown.
How does the sidebar behave when the admin panel is viewed on a smaller screen or a narrow viewport? The sidebar collapses gracefully without breaking the layout.
What happens if the admin's role does not have access to a specific section? The section is hidden from the sidebar and a 403 page is shown if accessed directly.
functionalRequirements: **FR-001**: The admin panel MUST include placeholder pages for all 9 primary sections: Dashboard Overview, User Management, Portfolio Management, Unit Management, Payments & Subscriptions, Reports & Analytics, Audit Logs, Notifications, and Settings.
**FR-002**: Each placeholder page MUST display the section title and a one-sentence description of its intended purpose.
**FR-003**: Each placeholder page MUST show a clear visual indicator (badge, banner, or illustration) communicating that the section is not yet fully implemented.
**FR-004**: The sidebar navigation MUST list all 9 sections and highlight the currently active section.
**FR-005**: Every placeholder page MUST include a header with a breadcrumb trail reflecting the current navigation path.
**FR-006**: All visible text MUST be served from translation files — no hardcoded strings are permitted.
**FR-007**: All placeholder pages MUST render correctly in both Arabic (RTL) and English (LTR).
**FR-008**: Direct URL access to any section MUST render the correct placeholder page without error.
**FR-009**: Navigation to a non-existent section MUST display a 404 error page consistent with the admin panel layout.
**FR-010**: Admin sections MUST be access-controlled; sections the logged-in admin role cannot access MUST be hidden from the sidebar and return a 403 page on direct URL access.
features.title: Feature Specification: Admin Dashboard Placeholder Pages
userStories: *Why this priority**: Without navigable placeholder pages, administrators have no way to explore the admin panel's scope or verify that routing is correctly wired. This is the foundation all subsequent admin features depend on.

*Independent Test**: Navigate to each of the 9 admin sections from the sidebar; every route renders a page without errors and displays a unique section title and a clear "coming soon" or "under construction" state. No section crashes, redirects unexpectedly, or shows a blank screen.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:

*Why this priority**: Placeholder pages that only show a title are confusing. A short description helps product owners, stakeholders, and QA understand the intended scope of each section during early demos.

*Independent Test**: Open each placeholder page and confirm it displays: (1) the section name, (2) a one-sentence description of the section's purpose, and (3) a visible "coming soon" indicator. Verify the description accurately matches the section.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: Consistent layout now prevents rework later. It also allows the admin panel to be demoed as a coherent product even before individual sections are built out.

*Independent Test**: Open every placeholder page and verify the sidebar, header, and breadcrumb trail are all present and consistent in structure and styling. Verify the breadcrumb correctly reflects the current section path.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:

*Why this priority**: The product targets the MENA region and Arabic is the default language. Placeholder pages that only work in English would fail the project's zero-hardcoded-strings rule from day one.

*Independent Test**: Toggle the interface language between Arabic and English. Verify all text on every placeholder page changes to the correct locale, the layout direction flips appropriately, and no untranslated strings are visible.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:

assumptions: The admin dashboard already has authenticated administrator accounts and role or permission concepts.
The first version focuses on app-wide preferences and operational configuration, not per-user personal preferences.
Only settings intentionally exposed for administration are editable; infrastructure-only configuration remains out of scope.
External service credentials are in scope only when they are explicitly modeled as sensitive settings and protected by separate permissions.
Existing audit or activity-log expectations apply to settings changes.
The settings page should be desktop-first, consistent with the admin dashboard, while still avoiding broken layouts on narrower screens.
The supported languages match the existing admin dashboard language set.
Maintenance mode closes the normal mobile app experience while preserving administrator access and any explicitly allowed operational bypass paths.
edgeCases: What happens when two administrators edit the same setting at nearly the same time? The later saver is warned that the setting changed and must review the latest value before saving.
What happens when saving partially fails? No partial configuration is applied unless the administrator is explicitly told which settings succeeded and which failed.
How does the page behave when settings cannot be loaded? The administrator sees a recoverable error state with a retry option and no stale editable form is presented as current.
What happens when a saved value takes effect later rather than immediately? The page states when the setting will become effective.
How are sensitive settings handled? Sensitive values are masked by default and only reveal or edit according to permission.
What happens when maintenance mode is enabled? The admin must provide user-facing maintenance copy and optional expected recovery time before the app can be closed to normal users.
What happens when external delivery or storage credentials are incomplete? The related integration is marked not ready and cannot be enabled as the active provider until required values are valid.
What happens when a mobile app version is blocked or a forced update is configured? The settings page explains which app versions are affected before saving.
functionalRequirements: **FR-001**: The admin dashboard MUST include an App Settings page reachable from the admin navigation by authorized administrators.
**FR-002**: The settings page MUST display configurable app preferences grouped by meaningful user-facing categories.
**FR-003**: Each setting MUST show a label, current effective value, description of its impact, editability status, and whether it is using a default or custom value.
**FR-004**: Authorized administrators MUST be able to edit supported settings using controls appropriate to the value type, such as toggles, selections, text, numbers, and dates.
**FR-005**: The system MUST validate setting values before applying changes and show field-specific validation errors for invalid entries.
**FR-006**: The system MUST prevent accidental loss of unsaved changes when an administrator cancels, navigates away, or reloads the page.
**FR-007**: The system MUST restrict settings viewing and editing according to administrator permissions.
**FR-008**: The system MUST record a change history for every successful settings update, including actor, timestamp, affected settings, previous values, and new values.
**FR-009**: Administrators MUST be able to search settings by label or description and filter settings by category.
**FR-010**: The settings page MUST provide a clear success confirmation after changes are saved and a clear recoverable error state when settings cannot be loaded or saved.
**FR-011**: The system MUST handle simultaneous edits by requiring administrators to review newer values before overwriting them.
**FR-012**: All visible settings page text MUST be available in the supported admin dashboard languages and respect the dashboard's text direction.
**FR-013**: Sensitive setting values MUST be masked by default and only viewable or editable by administrators with explicit permission.
**FR-014**: The page MUST identify settings whose changes are immediate, delayed, or require another operational action before taking effect.

**FR-015**: The settings catalog MUST include mail server configuration settings for provider choice, sender identity, host, port, encryption mode, username, password or secret, and delivery enablement.

**FR-016**: The settings catalog MUST include object storage settings for provider choice, endpoint or region, bucket or container name, access identity, secret credential, public URL or CDN base URL, and upload constraints.
**FR-017**: The settings catalog MUST include SMS and OTP gateway settings for provider choice, sender identity, credentials, OTP length, OTP expiry duration, retry limits, and resend cooldown.

**FR-018**: The settings catalog MUST include maintenance controls that allow authorized administrators to close the app to normal users, set maintenance message text, set optional expected recovery time, and allow privileged bypass access.

**FR-019**: The settings catalog MUST include mobile app baseline configuration for minimum supported app version, recommended app version, forced update behavior, app store links, feature availability flags, default locale, default country or region, timezone, currency, support contact, legal document links, and media upload limits.

**FR-020**: Settings that represent credentials or secrets MUST support update without requiring the current secret to be revealed, and history MUST record that the secret changed without exposing the secret value.
