**FR-021**: Administrators MUST be able to test or verify readiness of mail, SMS/OTP, and storage configuration before making the provider active when those settings are exposed as editable.

**FR-022**: The page MUST make high-impact settings, including maintenance mode, forced update, OTP policy, and active external provider changes, visibly distinct from routine preference changes before save.
features.title: Feature Specification: Admin App Settings Page
userStories: *Why this priority**: Administrators need a single trusted place to inspect operational preferences before they can safely manage them.

*Independent Test**: Sign in as an authorized administrator, open the settings page from the admin dashboard, and verify that all supported setting groups display their current values, descriptions, and editability status.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: The main value of the feature is allowing trusted administrators to control app behavior without engineering intervention.
*Independent Test**: Change one editable setting in each supported group, save the changes, reload the page, and verify that the saved values persist and are shown as the current values.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: App-wide configuration can affect all users, so access control and traceability are required for safe operations.

*Independent Test**: Compare the settings page as a settings manager and as a lower-privilege admin; verify edit controls are restricted and successful edits appear in the change history with actor, time, and changed fields.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: As app configuration grows, discoverability and plain-language descriptions prevent mistakes and reduce support needs.

*Independent Test**: Use search and grouping controls to find a specific preference by its user-facing label, description keyword, or category, then verify the page explains the setting's impact before editing.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:

assumptions: All new admin API endpoints required by this feature (e.g., `GET /admin/stats/dashboard`, `GET /admin/subscriptions`, `PATCH /admin/users/{id}/suspend`, `POST /admin/users/{id}/impersonate`, `GET /admin/content/developers`, etc.) will be built as part of this feature or are already available in the Laravel API.
The `admin_broadcasts` table and delivery-tracking columns exist or will be added as part of this feature's backend work.
Intercom or Crisp is not yet contracted; the Support → Tickets sub-page will initially embed a placeholder or a basic native ticket list based on whatever is available in the API.

Analytics data (funnel stages, retention) will be computed from existing tables (`profiles`, `units`, `installments`, `subscriptions`) via Laravel/Postgres aggregates — no third-party BI tool is required for the initial implementation.
The `translations` table already exists (per `docs/plan.md §14`) and is the authoritative store for dynamic strings.
The mobile app FAQ screen already reads from a `/faqs` API endpoint backed by the database; if it does not, that API endpoint must be added as part of this feature.
Impersonation will issue a short-lived (15-minute) Sanctum token scoped to the target user and clearly marked in the audit log; the admin does not gain a permanent credential.
Exchange rate sync for the Currencies sub-page reuses the existing `jobs:fx-sync` Artisan command triggered on-demand via a new admin API action.
edgeCases: What happens when an admin applies multiple filters simultaneously on the users list (plan + country + status)?
How does the system handle a broadcast notification when the target audience segment returns zero users?
What happens if an admin tries to impersonate a Super Admin account?
How does the system behave when a scheduled notification's dispatch time passes while the admin is still editing it?
What happens when a currency rate sync fails (external API unavailable)?
What if an admin competes with another admin saving the same app setting simultaneously (optimistic lock conflict)?
functionalRequirements: *Navigation & Shell**

**FR-001**: The sidebar MUST display all ten navigation sections without any "Coming Soon" badge or disabled state: Dashboard, Portfolios, Units, Installments, Checks, Documents, Users, Notifications, Audit Logs, Settings — and add Subscriptions, Content, Analytics, Support.
**FR-002**: Newly added sections (Subscriptions, Content, Analytics, Support) MUST appear in the sidebar with appropriate icons.
*Dashboard**
**FR-003**: The dashboard MUST display six KPI cards: Total Users, Monthly Active Users, Monthly Recurring Revenue, Active Subscriptions count, Churn Percentage, and Paid Users (Pro + Elite).
**FR-004**: The "Paid Users" count MUST be computed against all users in the system, not just the current paginated result set.
**FR-005**: The dashboard MUST include a user-growth line chart showing new registrations per week for the trailing 12 weeks.
**FR-006**: The dashboard MUST display a support tickets queue widget showing open ticket count and a link to the Support section.
*Users Management**
**FR-007**: The users list MUST support filtering by: plan (free/pro/elite/enterprise), country, account status (active/suspended), and signup date range — independently and in combination.
**FR-008**: The user detail page MUST display: total units count, lifetime revenue (sum of paid invoices), last active timestamp, and registered device platforms.

**FR-009**: The user detail page MUST offer an "Impersonate User" action that issues a scoped impersonation token and writes an audit log entry including the admin's ID, the target user's ID, and a timestamp.
**FR-010**: The user detail page MUST offer a "Suspend Account" toggle that blocks the user from authenticating and writes an audit log entry.
**FR-011**: The user detail page MUST offer an "Extend Trial" action that adds 14 days to the user's trial period.
**FR-012**: The user detail page MUST offer a "Force Reset Password" action that dispatches a password reset email.
**FR-013**: The subscription plan override form MUST include all four plans: free, pro, elite, enterprise.
*Subscriptions**
**FR-014**: A dedicated Subscriptions page MUST exist with three tabs: Active, Trialing, Churned.
**FR-015**: Each subscription row MUST show: user name/email, plan, status, provider (stripe/paymob/revenuecat/manual), and current period end date.
**FR-016**: Admins MUST be able to manually extend, comp, or initiate a refund on any subscription, with each action logged to audit logs.
**FR-017**: The subscriptions page MUST show a summary of MRR broken down by plan.
*Notifications**
**FR-018**: The broadcast notification form MUST have separate title and body fields for English and Arabic.
**FR-019**: The broadcast form MUST support audience targeting by: country, plan, and custom segment (users with N+ units, inactive N days).
**FR-020**: The broadcast form MUST support scheduling a send time (immediate or a future datetime).
**FR-021**: A template library MUST allow admins to save, name, and load notification templates that pre-fill the compose form.
**FR-022**: A notification history list MUST show past broadcasts with delivery statistics: sent count, delivered count, and opened count.
*Content Management**
**FR-023**: A Content section MUST contain sub-pages for: Countries, Currencies, Developers, Projects, and Translations.
**FR-024**: The Countries sub-page MUST allow enabling/disabling a country and editing its default currency and supported languages.
**FR-025**: The Currencies sub-page MUST display current exchange rates with a last-synced timestamp and a "Sync Now" button that triggers a manual rate refresh.
**FR-026**: The Developers sub-page MUST allow creating, editing, and verifying developer records including logo upload.
**FR-027**: The Projects sub-page MUST allow creating and editing verified project records linked to a developer, including delivery date and map coordinates.
**FR-028**: The Translations sub-page MUST allow inline editing of AR/EN values for every key in the `translations` database table, with changes taking effect immediately without a deployment.
*Analytics**
**FR-029**: An Analytics page MUST display a conversion funnel with four stages: registered → added first unit → logged first payment → upgraded plan.
**FR-030**: The Analytics page MUST display user retention cohorts grouped by signup month, showing the percentage of users still active in months 1, 2, and 3.
**FR-031**: The Analytics page MUST display a feature usage frequency table for the major features: units, payments, checks, documents, rentals.
*Support**
**FR-032**: A Support section MUST contain a FAQs sub-page allowing admins to create, edit, reorder, and delete FAQ items with AR and EN content fields.
**FR-033**: FAQ changes MUST be reflected in the mobile app FAQ screen without a code deployment.
**FR-034**: A Support section MUST contain a Tickets sub-page (direct integration with Intercom/Crisp embed, or a native ticket list linked to the conversations API).
*Audit & Security**
**FR-035**: Every admin action introduced by this feature (impersonate, suspend, extend trial, force reset, subscription override, content edits) MUST write a record to the `audit_logs` table.
**FR-036**: The audit logs list MUST link the actor field to the admin's user detail page.
features.title: Feature Specification: Admin Dashboard Completion
userStories: *Why this priority**: These pages are already built. Removing the badge costs minimal effort and immediately makes the panel functional for operational oversight.
*Independent Test**: Remove the `comingSoon: true` flags from all five entries. Navigate to each URL directly and confirm the pages load data from the API with no badge or disabled state.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: The dashboard is the first screen after login. Misleading or missing KPIs undermine trust in the platform's operational data.

*Independent Test**: Load the dashboard with a seeded dataset. Verify each of the six KPI cards shows the correct value, the Pro Users card reflects all users (not just the first page), and the growth chart renders with the correct data points.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: Without filters and actions, admins must scroll through hundreds of users to find the right record, and cannot take remediation actions without direct database access.

*Independent Test**: Apply a plan filter ("pro") on the users list and confirm only Pro users appear. On a user detail page, trigger "Suspend Account" and verify the user is blocked from signing in, with the action recorded in the audit log.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: Subscription management is core to the SaaS revenue model. Without it, Finance Admins have no operational control over billing edge cases.

*Independent Test**: Navigate to `/subscriptions`. Confirm three tabs appear (Active, Trialing, Churned). Select one subscription, click "Extend", set a new end date, and verify the change is reflected on the user detail page.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:

*Why this priority**: Content data (developers, projects, countries, translations) directly impacts the mobile app's catalog autocomplete and localization. Without an admin UI, every content update requires a database migration.

*Independent Test**: Add a new developer record via the Content → Developers sub-page. Navigate to Content → Projects and attach a project to that developer. Verify both appear as autocomplete options in a mobile app test session.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: The current form sends to all users or a single user ID with a single-language message. MENA SaaS operations require bilingual, targeted messaging.

*Independent Test**: Compose a notification targeted at plan = "free", country = "EG", in both EN and AR. Schedule it 10 minutes in the future. After the scheduled time passes, verify delivery stats show the correct sent/delivered counts.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: Analytics are needed for Phase 1.5 growth decisions but are not blocking day-to-day operations.

*Independent Test**: Load the Analytics page with seeded data spanning 4 cohort months. Confirm the funnel shows conversion percentages at each step and the retention table shows month-1 through month-3 retention rates per cohort.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: Support tooling is necessary for live operations but can be partially deferred to a later sprint if Intercom/Crisp integration is used externally.
*Independent Test**: Create a FAQ entry via the Support → FAQs sub-page. Open the mobile app and navigate to the support FAQs screen. Confirm the new entry appears.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:

assumptions: The Documents route is part of the existing admin dashboard navigation and shares the dashboard's admin authentication and authorization model.
Document upload itself is out of scope for this feature; this route reviews documents already uploaded elsewhere in the platform.
Deleting, replacing, or editing document metadata is out of scope for the first implementation unless already supported by existing admin flows.
Document file access uses temporary links so sensitive files are not exposed through permanent public URLs.
The first version supports type filtering and text search; advanced filters such as uploader, unit, date range, and file size can be added later.
Existing platform localization standards apply to all user-visible copy in the Documents route.
edgeCases: What happens when a document has missing optional metadata such as related unit name or uploader display name?

When a document's metadata exists but the file is missing from storage or a signed link cannot be generated, the detail page shows document metadata plus a localized file unavailable message and no download link.
What happens when a signed viewing link expires while the admin is still on the detail page?
How does pagination behave when the current page becomes empty after filters are applied?
What happens when an admin changes locale while viewing the Documents list or detail page?
functionalRequirements: **FR-001**: The admin sidebar MUST include a Documents navigation item that links to the Documents route and is not disabled.
**FR-002**: The Documents route MUST be accessible to authenticated admins and inaccessible to non-admin users.
**FR-003**: The Documents list page MUST display document name, type, formatted file size, related unit, uploader, and upload date for each visible document.
**FR-004**: The Documents list page MUST support an empty state when no documents are available or no records match the active filters.
**FR-005**: Admins MUST be able to filter the Documents list by the canonical document types: contract, receipt, title_deed, passport, national_id, and other.
**FR-006**: Admins MUST be able to search the Documents list by document name, document type, related unit name, related portfolio name, uploader name, and uploader email.
**FR-007**: The Documents list MUST support pagination for large result sets.
**FR-008**: Pagination controls MUST preserve active search and filter criteria.
**FR-009**: Each document row MUST provide a clear action to open the corresponding document detail view.
**FR-010**: The document detail view MUST display the selected document's metadata before offering file access.
**FR-011**: The document detail view MUST provide a time-limited file access link rather than a permanent public file URL.
**FR-012**: The detail view MUST show the expiration time for the file access link.
**FR-013**: The Documents route MUST provide localized English and Arabic text for titles, labels, filters, table headings, empty states, actions, and pagination controls.
**FR-014**: The Documents route MUST display correctly in left-to-right and right-to-left layouts.
**FR-015**: The Documents route MUST handle missing, deleted, or inaccessible documents with a user-friendly error state.
**FR-016**: Document metadata and file access MUST respect the same admin authorization rules as the rest of the admin dashboard.

**FR-017**: The system MUST write an audit log entry when an admin generates a temporary file access link from the document detail page; document list views and metadata detail views are not audit-logged by this feature.

**FR-018**: When document metadata exists but a temporary file access link cannot be generated, the detail view MUST still show available document metadata, display a localized file unavailable message, and hide the file access action.
features.title: Feature Specification: Admin Documents Route
userStories: *Why this priority**: The documents area is part of the core operational dashboard. Admins cannot verify uploaded contracts, receipts, or unit-related files if the route is hidden or blocked.
*Independent Test**: Sign in as an admin, select Documents from the sidebar, and confirm the Documents page loads with a localized title, subtitle, and document table area.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: Admin document review is useful only if staff can quickly understand what each file is and where it belongs.
*Independent Test**: Seed documents with different types, uploaders, and units. Load the Documents page and verify the list shows the expected metadata for each row.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: File volume grows with platform usage. Search and filtering keep the route useful once the document list becomes large.
*Independent Test**: Add documents with multiple names and types. Apply a type filter and search query, then confirm only matching results are shown and pagination keeps the selected filters.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: Uploaded documents may contain sensitive financial or ownership information. Admins need access, but links must remain controlled.
*Independent Test**: Select a document from the list, open its detail page, and confirm the view action provides a temporary file link with an expiry notice.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:

assumptions: The API backend is running and accessible at the configured `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL`; this spec does not change the API infrastructure.
The existing `AppSettingPolicy` authorization model is extended for new setting keys using the same pattern already applied to existing keys; no new permission types are introduced.
The `AppSettingSeeder` uses `updateOrCreate` on the `key` column, so re-running the seeder after the fix is idempotent and safe.
The current admin dashboard language set (Arabic and English) is unchanged; only those two locales need translation updates.
The integration readiness verify action is called on demand by the administrator (not on every page load) to avoid unnecessary API calls.
Group order and group descriptions remain as originally specified; only setting rows within existing groups are added or corrected.
edgeCases: What happens when the save action receives a conflict response alongside other validation errors? The conflict warning takes precedence; no partial changes are applied.
What happens when the settings page is opened and the API is not reachable? The recoverable error state with a retry button is shown; no stale form is displayed.
What happens when the readiness verify endpoint returns an error? The readiness badge shows an "Unknown" or "Error" state rather than silently failing.
What happens when seeded settings for newly added groups conflict with an existing row? The seeder uses `updateOrCreate` on the unique key, so existing rows are updated non-destructively.

What happens when an administrator tries to edit a setting that has no `allowed_values` for a `select` type? The select control renders with no options and the field appears broken; this is prevented by ensuring all seeded `select` settings have valid `allowed_values`.
functionalRequirements: **FR-001**: The save flow MUST parse field-level validation error messages returned by the API in the 422 response body and display each error message next to the corresponding form field.

**FR-002**: The admin API client MUST expose the response body of failed requests so that error-handling code in server actions can parse field errors, conflict details, and other structured failure payloads.
**FR-003**: The `AdminAppSettingsResponse` type MUST include the `readiness` field so that integration readiness summaries returned by the API are accessible in the frontend.
**FR-004**: The App Settings form MUST render an integration readiness status badge and a "Verify" action button for the Mail, SMS/OTP, and Storage group tabs when readiness data is available.
**FR-005**: The settings data seeder MUST include at least one setting entry for each of the three currently empty groups: Mobile App, Maintenance Mode, and Support and Legal.
**FR-006**: The Mobile App group MUST include settings for minimum supported app version, recommended app version, forced update behavior, default locale, and default currency.
**FR-007**: The Maintenance Mode group MUST include settings for a maintenance enabled toggle, a user-facing maintenance message text, and an optional expected recovery time.
**FR-008**: The Support and Legal group MUST include settings for support email address, support phone number, terms of service URL, and privacy policy URL.
**FR-009**: Boolean settings in read-only display mode MUST show "Enabled" or "Disabled" rather than "Default" or "Custom".

**FR-010**: The settings change history sidebar MUST display correctly for administrators who have history view permission; if the history list is empty the sidebar MUST show a descriptive empty state.
**FR-011**: The integration readiness verify server action MUST call the `/admin/settings/verify` endpoint and return the updated readiness status to the UI.
**FR-012**: All new setting keys added to the seeder MUST have corresponding translation entries in both `en.json` and `ar.json`.
**FR-013**: All new setting keys added to the seeder MUST be included in the `AppSettingPolicy` permission checks so they respect the existing authorization model.
**FR-014**: The settings page MUST remain free of TypeScript strict-mode errors after all fixes are applied.
features.title: Feature Specification: Fix Admin App Settings Pages
userStories: *Why this priority**: The primary purpose of the settings page is to allow administrators to change app configuration. If saving is broken, the entire feature has no value.
*Independent Test**: Log in as an admin, change at least one text, boolean, select, and integer setting, save, reload the page, and confirm every changed value is shown as the newly saved value.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:

*Why this priority**: Several groups currently have no settings seeded, making those tab panels empty. Administrators cannot configure mobile app versions, maintenance mode, or support links, which are core operational controls.
*Independent Test**: Open the settings page and click each group tab. Every tab must show at least one setting entry with a label, value, and description.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:

*Why this priority**: Administrators need confidence that external delivery and storage integrations are correctly configured before enabling them. The readiness UI was specified and the API endpoint exists but is never shown in the current UI.

*Independent Test**: Open the settings page, navigate to the Mail, SMS/OTP, or Storage group, and verify that a readiness status indicator is visible. Set all required credentials and trigger a verify action; confirm the status updates to ready.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:

*Why this priority**: The current implementation returns a generic "Validation error occurred" message for all 422 responses from the API. Administrators cannot act on a generic message; they need to know which field failed and why.

assumptions: "Developers" in this feature refers exclusively to real estate development companies (e.g., Emaar, Palm Hills), not software developers.
"Projects" refers to real estate developments or compounds (e.g., "Palm Hills October"), not software projects.
The admin panel already has authentication and role-based access control in place; this feature does not alter authorization rules beyond what already exists.
The mobile app and web clients will pass `lang` as a URL query parameter, not as an HTTP header.
Only two languages are in scope: Arabic (`ar`) and English (`en`). No other locales will be added in this iteration.
Both the Arabic and English translations are required fields — a record cannot be published without both translations filled.
Currency codes follow ISO 4217 (e.g., EGP, USD, SAR) and must be unique across the system.
Soft deletion (flagging records as inactive) is acceptable for cases where hard deletion is blocked by dependencies, but the initial implementation will use hard deletion with dependency checks.
Exchange rates for currencies are out of scope for this feature (handled by the existing fx-sync job).
Developer logos and additional media assets are out of scope for the initial implementation; only text fields are required.
edgeCases: What happens when an admin saves a record with the Arabic translation filled but the English translation left blank — does the system reject or save with a warning?
How does the system handle an API client that passes `lang` in the request header vs. query string — only query string is supported per this spec.
What happens if a developer is renamed while a project is actively being edited — last save wins per standard CRUD behavior.
What happens when a currency code (e.g., EGP) already exists and the admin tries to create another with the same code — the system must reject with a clear duplicate error.
functionalRequirements: **FR-001**: System MUST allow admins to create currencies with a unique code, symbol, Arabic name, and English name.
**FR-002**: System MUST allow admins to edit any field of an existing currency.
**FR-003**: System MUST prevent deletion of currencies that are referenced by any existing unit, portfolio, or financial record, and display a clear reason with dependency count.
**FR-004**: System MUST allow deletion of currencies with no dependencies.
**FR-005**: System MUST allow admins to create real estate developers with an Arabic name and an English name (both required).
**FR-006**: System MUST allow admins to edit any field of an existing developer.
**FR-007**: System MUST prevent deletion of developers that have associated projects, and display a clear reason.
**FR-008**: System MUST allow deletion of developers with no associated projects.
**FR-009**: System MUST allow admins to create real estate projects with Arabic name, English name, Arabic description, English description, and a linked developer (required).
**FR-010**: System MUST allow admins to edit any field of an existing project.
**FR-011**: System MUST prevent deletion of projects that have associated units, and display a clear reason.
**FR-012**: System MUST allow deletion of projects with no associated units.
**FR-013**: All API endpoints for currencies, developers, and projects MUST accept a `lang` query parameter with values `ar` or `en`.
**FR-014**: When `lang=en` is passed, API responses MUST return English translations for all translatable text fields.
**FR-015**: When `lang=ar` is passed (or no `lang` is passed), API responses MUST return Arabic translations for all translatable text fields.
**FR-016**: When an unsupported `lang` value is passed, the system MUST fall back to Arabic without returning an error.
**FR-017**: Admin MUST be able to list all currencies, developers, and projects with pagination and search/filter by name.
**FR-018**: All admin create, update, and delete operations MUST be recorded in the audit log.

userStories: *Why this priority**: Currencies are foundational reference data. All unit prices, installment amounts, and financial figures depend on a valid currency list. Without this, investors cannot accurately track their portfolios in the correct currency context.

*Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by navigating to the Currencies section in the admin dashboard, creating a new currency with both AR and EN names, then calling the API with `lang=ar` and `lang=en` to confirm the correct name appears in each response. Delivers: a working currency list that investors see in their language.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: Developers are required reference data for projects — a project cannot exist without an associated developer. Fixing developer management unlocks project management.

*Why this priority**: Projects are the second tier of reference data — units are associated with projects. Without project management, investors cannot correctly categorize their holdings.

*Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by creating a project in the admin dashboard (with a developer already set up), then calling the projects API with `lang=ar` and `lang=en` to confirm the project details are returned correctly in both languages.

*Why this priority**: This is the core i18n requirement. Without it, investors always see content in one language regardless of their preference, breaking the bilingual promise of the platform.

assumptions: The admin panel already has an App Settings section (from spec 016-admin-app-settings); this feature extends it with a new "Integrations" sub-section.
The mobile app already handles Google and Apple sign-in flows; this feature provides the server-side credential storage so those flows can be activated.
Client API key enforcement is applied at the API gateway layer — all routes require the key header, with no per-route opt-out needed at this stage.
Only one active client API key is needed at a time (single key per environment); multi-key support for zero-downtime rotation is out of scope for this version.
Apple Sign-In private key is provided as pasted text (PEM format), not a file upload widget, to keep the implementation simple.
Payment gateway keys (Stripe, Paymob) and push notification credentials are in scope as future integrations but are not implemented in this feature.
All settings in this feature are global (not per-tenant); they apply to the entire application.
The Integration Guide tab is read-only; it displays values but does not allow editing them in-place (edits happen in their respective credential sections).
The Integration Guide tab is visible only to admin users; it is not accessible to tenant users or unauthenticated visitors.
edgeCases: What happens when an admin saves credentials with leading/trailing whitespace?
How does the system behave when a third-party service returns an auth error due to misconfigured credentials?
What if an admin revokes the only active client API key while the mobile app is in production?
How are settings changes reflected — immediately (live reload) or after a manual cache clear / app restart?
What happens if the private key for Apple Sign-In is uploaded in an unsupported format?
What happens on the Integration Guide tab when the clipboard API is unavailable (e.g., non-HTTPS context)?
Should the Integration Guide tab be accessible to non-admin roles (e.g., a developer with read-only access)?
functionalRequirements: **FR-001**: System MUST allow admins to generate new client API keys from the settings panel.
**FR-002**: System MUST display a newly generated client API key exactly once in full; all subsequent views MUST show only a masked version (e.g., last 4 characters).
**FR-003**: System MUST allow admins to revoke any active client API key, rendering it immediately invalid.
**FR-004**: System MUST warn admins before regenerating or revoking a production key, requiring explicit confirmation.
**FR-005**: System MUST reject any API request that does not carry a valid, active client API key.
**FR-006**: System MUST allow admins to configure Google Sign-In by providing a Client ID and Client Secret.
**FR-007**: System MUST allow admins to enable or disable each sign-in provider independently.
**FR-008**: System MUST allow admins to configure Apple Sign-In by providing Team ID, Key ID, and private key content.
**FR-009**: System MUST allow admins to store a Google Maps API key.
**FR-010**: System MUST strip leading and trailing whitespace from all credential inputs before saving.
**FR-011**: System MUST mask all sensitive credential values (secrets, private keys, API keys) in all UI views after initial creation.
**FR-012**: System MUST log every settings change (who changed what and when) to the audit log.
**FR-013**: System MUST apply settings changes for sign-in providers without requiring a server restart.

**FR-014**: Admin MUST have an extensible integration panel — the UI architecture MUST support adding new integration types (e.g., push notification keys, payment gateway keys) without rebuilding the page.
**FR-015**: System MUST provide a dedicated "Client Integration" tab within the Settings panel that consolidates all information a developer needs to connect a client app to the API.
**FR-016**: The Integration Guide tab MUST display the current API base URL and the active client API key (masked) with a one-click copy-to-clipboard action for each value.

**FR-017**: The Integration Guide tab MUST present connection setup as a numbered, step-by-step guide covering: required headers, authentication method, environment configuration, and verification steps.
**FR-018**: The Integration Guide tab MUST reflect the live, current values (base URL, active key) — it MUST NOT show stale data after a key rotation or URL change.
**FR-019**: When no client API key has been generated, the Integration Guide tab MUST display a clear prompt and direct action to generate one, rather than showing an empty or broken state.

acceptanceScenarios: **Admins** maintain the *reference data* that benchmarks depend on — gold prices, exchange rates, inflation rates, area price indices, developer intelligence scores, project analytics, and the scoring weights.
**Investors** consume *computed analytics* for their own units — real (inflation-adjusted) ROI, gold/USD benchmarks, area growth, annualized return, and an overall 0–100 investment score.
assumptions: **Areas**: A new canonical Areas reference (city → district) is introduced; existing free-text `area`/`city` values on units will be mapped to canonical areas (mapping/cleanup is part of this feature's data work).
**Analytics surface**: Metrics are computed once on the server and exposed via the API, then surfaced in both the investor mobile app and the admin panel (no client-side recomputation).
**Exchange rates**: The Currency Exchange Rates section reuses/extends the existing `currency_rates` data and the FX-sync job rather than introducing a parallel FX store.

**Score normalization** (default, tunable later): each weighted component is normalized to a 0–100 sub-score using a defined linear scale with caps (e.g., ROI/area-growth mapped against target bands; risk inverted so lower risk scores higher), then combined by the configured weights. The exact normalization curves will be finalized in planning and are not hardcoded into the spec.
**Gold purity for benchmark**: the gold benchmark uses 24k price per gram by default; 21k is stored for reference and possible future configurability.

**Total cost**: "total cost" for ROI uses the recorded purchase price (plus any captured acquisition costs already modeled), and "current value" uses the most recent valuation; if no valuation exists, the view prompts for one rather than assuming a value.

**Period fallback**: when an exact period is missing in a reference series, the nearest prior available period is used and disclosed; if none exists before the relevant date, the metric is "insufficient data."
**Authorization**: investor analytics are tenant-scoped to owned/invited units; all admin sections require admin access via the existing policy/Gate model and write to the audit log.
**Currency normalization**: all benchmark math is performed in a consistent base currency, converting unit values via the exchange-rate data where needed.
**Excel format**: a documented column template is provided for each importable dataset; imports are validated server-side.
edgeCases: **Holding period < 1 year**: annualized return must handle sub-year periods without overstating returns; very short periods (days) should be flagged rather than annualized into extreme figures.

**Missing reference data**: gaps in gold/FX/inflation/area-index series for the relevant dates → metric shows "insufficient data"; nearest-available-period fallback rules must be explicit and disclosed to the user.
**No current value recorded**: ROI and score cannot be computed; the view prompts to add a valuation rather than assuming purchase price.
**Currency mismatch**: unit purchased in a currency other than the base currency must be normalized consistently before benchmarking.
**Duplicate periods on import**: same date (gold/FX) or same month/year (inflation) or same area+type+period (index) must be detected and resolved (skip vs. update), never silently duplicated.
**Weights not summing to 100%**: scoring configuration must be rejected.
**Negative / zero values**: zero or negative purchase price, or negative prices in imports, must be rejected with clear validation.
**Future-dated periods**: market data dated in the future should be rejected or clearly flagged.
**Score with a missing component**: define whether the weight is dropped and the remainder re-normalized, or the score is marked "partial."

userStories: *Why this priority**: Every downstream benchmark (real ROI, gold benchmark, USD benchmark) is impossible without this data. It is the foundation and delivers value on its own — admins gain a single, auditable source of macro-economic reference data.

*Independent Test**: Seed an empty environment, have an admin add several months of gold/FX/inflation rows (manually and via Excel import), filter by date range, and confirm the historical chart renders the entered series. No investor-facing analytics required to validate.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: This is the headline goal — letting investors judge whether a property genuinely beat inflation, gold, and the dollar. It is the primary value delivered to end users.

*Independent Test**: With reference data and a scoring configuration seeded, open a unit that has a purchase price, purchase date, and current value, and verify each metric and the overall score compute to expected values; change the current value and confirm metrics update.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:

*Why this priority**: Powers the "area growth" metric in US2 and gives investors a market benchmark for their location. Needed for complete analytics but US2 can ship partially without it (area growth shows "insufficient data").

*Independent Test**: Create a few areas, add price-per-meter points across several periods and property types, import a batch via Excel, and confirm the growth chart shows the trend per area/property type.

assumptions: This is an umbrella specification: implementation is delivered through a sequence of follow-up features (per the roadmap in `docs/saas-engine-implementation-plan.md` §25–26), each independently specified, planned, and shipped. OAR B remains a working product throughout and is the first reference product on the engine.

The architecture remains a modular monolith: one deployable backend and one transactional database. Microservices, per-module databases, generic user-defined entities, and publishing the engine as public packages are explicitly out of scope for Engine v1.

Every existing user receives exactly one automatically created personal organization. Organization-unaware legacy clients always use that personal organization; organization-aware clients may explicitly select another verified active organization.

Portfolio-level collaboration remains in place during the compatibility period and restricts migrated collaborator access within the organization to the same portfolios as before; whether selective portfolio access persists long-term as a product feature is a deferred product decision.

Existing clients (current mobile and admin releases) continue working through compatibility behavior until they are explicitly migrated; deprecation signals are introduced only when clients are ready.

The second-product pilot is a deliberately small business vertical slice (the plan suggests clinic operations); its exact domain is chosen when that phase begins and does not affect engine requirements.

Stabilizing the current baseline (the known failing automated checks and obsolete architecture guidance recorded in the plan's current-state analysis) is the first phase of this program, not a separate effort.
Current plan tiers (Free, Pro, Elite, Enterprise) and their existing limits are carried into the capability catalog unchanged; no commercial repricing is part of this transformation.
edgeCases: A user belongs to multiple organizations: every request must resolve one verified active organization; ambiguous requests are rejected rather than guessed, and clients offer explicit organization selection.
A request arrives with no resolvable organization context (e.g., a token from a deleted organization): the request is refused with a stable, distinguishable error rather than acting on a default.
A user from another organization guesses or enumerates resource identifiers: the response must not reveal whether the resource exists.
Two simultaneous requests compete for the last remaining slot of a limited capability: exactly one may succeed; the system must never over-allocate.

A payment event arrives for an organization that is suspended, pending deletion, or unknown: the event is retained for reconciliation and processed idempotently; it is never silently dropped or applied to the wrong tenant.
A data backfill is interrupted (crash, timeout, operator stop): it must resume from a recorded position, remain idempotent, and produce a failure/reconciliation report.
The sole owner of an organization deletes their account: ownership must be transferred or the organization explicitly wound down; the system must not orphan an organization silently.

An organization enters pending deletion: access is blocked, authorized owners may restore it for 30 days, and after that window tenant data is permanently purged. Retained billing and audit rows contain only the fields listed in FR-003, carry a retention-expiry timestamp from the product compliance schedule, and are deleted by an auditable scheduled purge when that timestamp passes.
A module is disabled for a product while organizations still hold its data: the data is preserved; only access paths (navigation, endpoints) are removed.
An entitlement override expires or the plan changes mid-period: effective limits recalculate immediately and predictably (most permissive of plan vs. active override).

A plan downgrade or expired override leaves current usage above the effective limit: existing resources remain accessible and are never deleted automatically, but creation and usage increases are refused until consumption falls within the limit.

An older client version that predates organizations calls a legacy endpoint: the platform resolves the user's migration-created personal organization and the request behaves as before; it cannot implicitly access another organization.

A suspended organization's scheduled notifications and reminders: delivery is withheld while suspended; time-sensitive notifications (e.g., payment due reminders) scheduled during suspension are discarded upon suspension detection, not queued for post-restoration delivery; recurring notifications (e.g., weekly digests) resume their normal schedule when the organization is restored.
Platform support staff need to inspect a customer's data to resolve a ticket: access requires an explicit, time-bounded, reasoned grant and every access is audited.

Customer approval cannot be obtained during a security or availability incident: only a designated platform security administrator may issue a time-bounded emergency grant, with the reason, scope, actor, and all resulting access recorded for review.
functionalRequirements: *Tenancy and Organizations**

**FR-001**: The system MUST make the organization the unit of tenant ownership: every tenant-owned record is traceable to exactly one organization, directly or through an explicit parent relationship.

**FR-002**: The system MUST automatically create an organization for every existing user and migrate their portfolios and collaborators into it with no user action and no behavior change; migrated collaborators MUST become organization members while retained portfolio-level permissions continue to restrict them to the portfolios they could previously access. Existing subscription benefits MUST remain unchanged through compatibility reads until FR-016 migrates subscription ownership.

**FR-003**: Users MUST be able to create an organization and manage its profile, defaults (language, currency, timezone), and lifecycle states (active, suspended, pending deletion, deleted). An organization in pending deletion MUST be restorable by an authorized owner for 30 days; after 30 days, its tenant data MUST be permanently purged. Retention after purge is limited to: (a) the minimized organization identifier and terminal deletion timestamps required for referential integrity; (b) billing transaction identifiers, provider, monetary amount/currency, tax/invoice reference, transaction/status timestamps, and organization identifier, with customer names, emails, phone numbers, addresses, free text, and provider payloads removed; and (c) immutable audit event identifier, actor pseudonymous identifier, organization identifier, action, subject type/pseudonymous identifier, correlation identifier, event timestamp, and redacted before/after metadata, with IP address, user agent, secrets, contact data, and unrelated payload fields removed. For the initial Egypt product schedule, billing records MUST expire 7 years after the later of transaction creation or organization purge, and retained audit records MUST expire 7 years after event creation. Each retained row MUST carry or resolve to a retention-expiry timestamp, and a scheduled idempotent purge MUST permanently delete expired retained rows and write a non-personal reconciliation record. Product jurisdiction/configuration MAY select a different versioned schedule only after documented legal/data-controller approval.

**FR-004**: Organization owners and admins MUST be able to invite people by role, and invitees MUST be able to accept or decline; owners MUST be able to remove members and transfer ownership. Minimum roles: owner, admin, member, viewer.

**FR-005**: The system MUST resolve and verify the active organization on the server for every tenant-scoped request; identifiers supplied by a client MUST never establish tenancy without membership validation, and requests without valid organization context MUST be refused. For organization-unaware legacy clients, the server MUST resolve tenant context only to the user's migration-created personal organization. Access to any other organization MUST require an organization-aware client that explicitly selects a verified active organization.
**FR-006**: The system MUST prevent all cross-organization data access; attempts MUST be refused without revealing resource existence.
*Authorization and Roles**

**FR-007**: The system MUST separate platform-level roles (e.g., super admin, operations, support, finance, content) from organization-level roles; the two MUST be independently assignable and testable.
**FR-008**: Every protected operation MUST be governed by a named permission following a uniform `<module>.<resource>.<action>` naming scheme, and each module MUST declare its permission catalog.

**FR-009**: Platform staff access to tenant data MUST be explicit and audited. Routine support access MUST be approved by an organization owner and carry a reason, scope, and expiration. When customer approval cannot be obtained during a security or availability incident, only a designated platform security administrator MAY issue an emergency grant; the grant and every resulting access MUST be recorded for review.
*Plans, Entitlements, and Usage**
**FR-010**: The system MUST maintain a catalog of capabilities supporting these types:
**Boolean access**: a feature that is either enabled or disabled for an organization (no numeric limit).
**Numeric limit**: a maximum count of a resource an organization may hold (e.g., units, portfolios); consumption is tracked as current count versus limit; resets only when resources are deleted.
**Metered usage**: a consumption budget that depletes with use and resets on a defined billing-period boundary (e.g., exports per month); tracks used versus allowance within the period.
**Storage allowance**: a maximum total size of stored objects (files, attachments) measured in bytes; consumption is the sum of stored object sizes versus the limit.
**Retention period**: a maximum duration for which records of a given category are retained before scheduled purge; measured from the record's creation or reference event timestamp.
**FR-011**: Plans MUST be defined per product as data (capability assignments with limits), and adding a new capability or plan MUST NOT require changes to the shared enforcement engine.

**FR-012**: Usage MUST be tracked per organization per capability, with consumption that is atomic (concurrent requests can never exceed a limit) and idempotent (repeating a recorded consumption has no additional effect).
**FR-013**: When an action is refused for entitlement reasons, the response MUST carry a stable machine-readable code and identify the capability, the limit, and current usage.
**FR-014**: Platform administrators MUST be able to apply per-organization entitlement overrides, with a complete history of who changed what, when, and why.

**FR-015**: Rollout flags (whether an implementation is currently enabled for a target) MUST be distinct from entitlements (whether a customer is allowed the capability); an action MAY require both. When a plan change or override expiry lowers an effective limit below current usage, the system MUST preserve access to existing resources and MUST block creation or other usage increases until consumption returns within the effective limit; it MUST NOT automatically disable or delete excess resources.
*Billing**
**FR-016**: Subscriptions MUST belong to organizations; existing user-owned subscriptions MUST be migrated to the owner's organization with benefits preserved.

**FR-017**: Payment events from every supported provider MUST resolve to the correct organization and be processed exactly once, including under duplicate delivery; provider-specific details MUST NOT leak beyond the normalization boundary.
**FR-018**: Administrators MUST be able to manage organization subscriptions (extend, grant complimentary periods, override, refund), and every such action MUST be audited.
*Domain-Neutral Platform Services**

**FR-019**: File storage MUST be domain-neutral, identifying files by organization, owning module, resource type and identifier, category, and visibility; files MUST be private by default, served through time-limited access links, and organization membership MUST be validated before access is granted. Existing documents and images MUST continue to work throughout the transition.

**FR-020**: Notifications MUST be requested through a domain-neutral mechanism (recipient, template, language, channels, deduplication key, optional schedule) supporting push, email, and in-app channels through interchangeable providers, honoring user preferences, and recording delivery attempts. Existing reminders, risk alerts, and digests MUST keep working.

**FR-021**: Audit records MUST capture actor, organization context, action, subject, before/after snapshots, request metadata, and a correlation identifier. Audit records MUST be append-only and unmodifiable until their applicable retention-expiry timestamp, after which only the scheduled deletion required by FR-003 may remove them; duplicate audit entries for a single operation MUST be eliminated.

**FR-022**: Settings MUST support platform, product, organization, and user scopes with a documented resolution order (user → organization → product → platform default), validation, optimistic version-conflict detection (concurrent updates to the same setting key and scope are rejected with a version mismatch error), change history, and protection of sensitive values.
*Modularity and Product Configuration**

**FR-023**: Every data collection, endpoint, and published event MUST have exactly one declared owning module; other modules MUST access it only through public contracts, events, or explicitly approved read interfaces.
**FR-024**: The shared platform foundation (kernel) MUST contain no references to any specific business domain's concepts; violations MUST be detected by automated checks that fail the build.

**FR-025**: The existing real-estate functionality MUST be packaged as a self-contained domain module that a product can enable or disable; disabling it MUST remove its navigation and endpoints without affecting platform capabilities or preserved data.

**FR-026**: Every product MUST be described by a validated manifest selecting enabled modules, navigation, branding, locales, default country/currency, providers, and plan definitions; the manifest MUST NOT bypass authorization or entitlements, store secrets, or define executable business logic.

**FR-027**: Every module MUST declare machine-readable metadata — dependencies, permissions, capabilities, settings, published and consumed events — and this metadata MUST drive validation, documentation, and product diagnostics.

**FR-028**: Cross-module side effects MUST flow through versioned events carrying stable identifiers; consumers MUST tolerate replay (idempotent handling). The event envelope format, naming convention (`<module>.<event>.v<N>`), and versioning rules are defined in `contracts/kernel-events.md`.
*Tooling and Diagnostics**

**FR-029**: A product generator MUST produce a working product scaffold including authentication, organization onboarding, member invitations, base roles, subscription scaffolding, settings, notifications, file storage, audit logging, localization structure, a development environment, and quality gates.
**FR-030**: A module generator MUST produce a complete domain-module scaffold (backend structure, client feature structure, translations, test templates, documentation template, module metadata).

**FR-031**: A product diagnostic MUST report missing or inconsistent product configuration (manifest validity, module dependencies, missing permissions, capabilities, translations, provider configuration) before release.

**FR-032**: Automated boundary validation MUST fail the build when ownership or dependency rules are violated (platform depending on a domain, one domain reaching into another's internals, undeclared permissions/capabilities/events).
*Migration Safety and Compatibility**

**FR-033**: Existing public interfaces and client behavior MUST be preserved throughout the transformation; breaking changes are allowed only through an explicitly versioned release. (See also SC-002 for the regression-suite verification criterion.)

**FR-034**: Every critical data migration MUST follow an expand → backfill → reconcile → switch → enforce sequence, and every backfill MUST support dry run, batching, resumption, idempotency, progress reporting, and a reconciliation report. (See also `tasks.md` Conventions for implementers for the operational application of this sequence.)

**FR-035**: The transformation MUST begin from a verified green baseline: all currently known failing automated checks are fixed and obsolete architecture guidance is removed before structural work starts.
*Governance**

**FR-036**: All feature specifications and architecture documents MUST carry a lifecycle status (draft, active, implemented, superseded, archived), and every module MUST have documentation covering its purpose, boundaries, owned data, contracts, permissions, capabilities, events, and operational notes.

**FR-037**: The engine is validated only when a second product in a different business domain delivers a working vertical slice reusing at least 80% of platform capabilities without copying or forking engine code. **Reuse ratio definition**: reuse % = (reused kernel/platform capabilities) ÷ (reused kernel/platform capabilities + pilot-specific capabilities) × 100. Before pilot implementation begins, the feature 036 specification and plan MUST freeze a reviewed capability inventory containing every runtime capability required by the vertical slice. At minimum, the inventory MUST separately enumerate authentication, organization onboarding/context, invitations/membership, authorization, entitlement/usage enforcement, notifications, files, audit, subscription/billing, and each pilot-domain capability. A capability counts as reused only when the pilot consumes an existing kernel contract, event, or service unchanged with zero copied or forked engine code; wrappers that reproduce kernel behavior count as pilot-specific. The reuse report MUST map every inventory item to evidence, include all pilot-specific capabilities in the denominator, and record approval of the frozen inventory before T167 starts.

userStories: *Why this priority**: Protecting the live product is the non-negotiable constraint of the entire transformation. If existing customers experience breakage or data loss, the engine effort fails regardless of its architectural merit. Every later story builds on this migration being safe.

*Independent Test**: Run the full existing-product regression suite against a migrated environment seeded with production-like data. All current workflows (authentication, portfolio management, payments tracking, documents, notifications, exports, subscription management) pass unchanged, and a reconciliation report confirms every user, portfolio, and collaborator is correctly mapped to an organization while subscription benefits remain unchanged through compatibility reads.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:

*Why this priority**: The organization is the new tenant boundary on which authorization, billing, entitlements, and every future product depend. It is the first net-new capability the engine must deliver after the safe migration.

*Independent Test**: Create a fresh organization, invite a second user in each role, and verify the full isolation matrix: owners and permitted members can act, members without permission are refused, users from another organization cannot see or guess their way into the data, and a suspended organization blocks all member access.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:

*Why this priority**: Capability-based entitlements replace hard-coded plan checks and are what allows every future product to define its own plans without modifying shared enforcement logic. They are also a direct revenue-protection mechanism.

*Independent Test**: Define a plan with one boolean capability and one limited capability through configuration only, assign it to a test organization, and verify allowed/denied behavior at, below, and beyond the limit — including two simultaneous requests competing for the final slot — without any change to enforcement code.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: Billing must align with the tenant boundary so teams can share one subscription and future products can bill businesses. It depends on Stories 1–3 being in place.

*Independent Test**: Migrate a user-owned subscription to its organization, simulate provider payment events (success, renewal, cancellation, duplicate delivery), and verify the correct organization's entitlements update exactly once per event; verify admin subscription actions appear in the audit log.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:

*Why this priority**: This is the heart of "being a SaaS engine": separating the reusable platform from the business domain so the same foundation can power different products. It requires the kernel capabilities from earlier stories to exist first.

*Independent Test**: Represent OAR B itself as a complete product manifest. Validate that the assembled product exposes exactly the configured modules and navigation, that an invalid manifest (e.g., enabling a module without its dependencies) is rejected before the product can start, and that the manifest cannot grant access that authorization or entitlements would deny.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:

*Why this priority**: Generators and a second-product validation are the payoff of the transformation — they make the engine fast to use and prove it is genuinely reusable. They are last because they depend on everything before them.

*Independent Test**: Generate a new product and a new module from scratch, confirm both pass all baseline quality checks, intentionally break a boundary rule and confirm the build fails, then deliver the second-product vertical slice (onboarding, invitation, one domain resource with create/read/update/delete, one limited capability, one notification, one file attachment, audit trail, subscription change) measuring the reuse ratio.

assumptions: ClinicFlow targets clinic operations administration (scheduling, patients, billing, staffing); it is not an electronic health record system and stores demo-grade clinical data without regulated-PHI ambitions in this scope.
The existing appointments domain (`domain.clinic-operations` from the 036 pilot) is reused and extended rather than rebuilt; patients, invoicing, and staff scheduling are new domain modules.
All kernel capabilities (identity, organizations, authorization/roles, billing, entitlements, settings, feature flags, notifications, files, audit) are consumed unchanged from the engine.
Payments are handled via the engine's web payment provider (international/USD context); no clinic-specific payment integration is in scope.
"Clinic" maps to the engine's organization concept; staff map to invited organization members; no new tenancy primitive is introduced.
Reminder lead time and exact monthly allowance numbers per tier are product configuration to be finalized in planning, not fixed requirements here.
The minimal `clinic` pilot stays selectable and frozen; ClinicFlow supersedes it as the real product without a rename sweep.
edgeCases: What happens when a clinic at its allowance tries to book/issue at the exact boundary, and two staff act concurrently? The total must never exceed the allowance.
How does the system handle a cancelled appointment whose reminder has already fired vs. not yet fired?
How does the system handle an attachment upload that fails partway — no orphan record is left referencing a missing file.
What happens to a patient's attachments and invoices when a clinic is suspended? Access is blocked while suspended, data is retained.
How does an invoice behave if its linked appointment/visit is later cancelled?
A staff member's role is downgraded mid-session — subsequent privileged actions are denied.
functionalRequirements: *Product & tenancy**
**FR-001**: System MUST expose ClinicFlow as a distinct product, selectable independently of OAR B and the `clinic` pilot, with its own identity, branding theme, and analytics namespace.

**FR-002**: System MUST default to English (LTR) with United States region defaults (USD), while also offering Arabic as a secondary locale; locale and direction MUST be product configuration, not built-in assumptions.
**FR-003**: Every clinic MUST be an organization (tenant); every clinic resource (appointments, patients, invoices, availability) MUST be scoped to its clinic and isolated from all other clinics.
**FR-004**: System MUST allow a clinic owner to invite staff by email and have invitees join the clinic as members with role-scoped access.
**FR-005**: Every authenticated clinic action MUST be authorized by role; unauthorized and foreign-clinic access MUST be denied as if the resource does not exist.
**FR-006**: System MUST record every clinic state change (appointment, patient, invoice, availability mutations; status transitions; subscription changes) in the clinic's audit trail.
*Appointments**
**FR-007**: Staff MUST be able to create, reschedule, and cancel appointments scoped to their clinic.
**FR-008**: System MUST schedule a reminder ahead of each appointment and suppress/cancel that reminder when the appointment is cancelled.

**FR-009**: System MUST enforce a per-clinic monthly appointment allowance defined by the clinic's plan; bookings beyond the allowance MUST be refused with a machine-readable limit-exceeded result and an upgrade prompt, and the allowance MUST never be exceeded under concurrency.
*Patients & attachments**
**FR-010**: Staff MUST be able to create and maintain patient records scoped to their clinic.
**FR-011**: Staff MUST be able to attach documents to a patient or visit; attachments MUST be stored privately and served only to authorized clinic members via time-limited links.
*Billing / invoicing**
**FR-012**: Billers MUST be able to issue invoices linked to an appointment/visit, scoped to their clinic, and track status transitions (draft, issued, paid).

**FR-016**: System MUST ship ClinicFlow plan tiers (free, standard, pro) whose monthly allowances for appointments and invoices increase by tier.
**FR-017**: System MUST allow a clinic to change its subscription tier, applying the new allowances, and handle an above-limit downgrade per the engine's established downgrade behavior.

**FR-018**: ClinicFlow MUST be assembled from the engine using the product and module generators; it MUST NOT fork or copy any kernel implementation.

**FR-020**: Every new ClinicFlow endpoint MUST be documented and covered by both policy/behavior tests and black-box integration tests; the product MUST pass the engine's diagnostics and boundary validation.

assumptions: "Admin dashboard" refers to the `apps/admin` web console (admin, engine, and product surfaces) and not the mobile app.

"Keep use i18n but only for En" means: retain the translation-key indirection and catalog mechanism, ship/load only the English catalog, and remove the Arabic catalog from the admin's runtime — not remove i18n entirely.

Arabic *data values* stored in domain records (e.g., `name_ar`, translation entries) are content, not UI localization, and remain viewable/manageable; only the admin *UI chrome* is constrained to English LTR.
The mobile app and any shared i18n packages must keep their Arabic support intact for mobile; this feature only changes what the admin consumes.
Removing per-locale routing/branching for the admin is acceptable; a single canonical (English/LTR) route structure is the target, with redirects from old locale-prefixed URLs.
The constitution update is performed via the project's constitution workflow as a follow-up step; this spec defines the rules that workflow must encode.
Re-introducing additional admin locales later is not a goal of this feature, but keeping the i18n catalog mechanism leaves that path open without rework.
edgeCases: **Stale Arabic/RTL URLs and bookmarks**: Requests to old `ar` locale paths must resolve to the English LTR experience without a broken page or 404.

**Arabic data fields**: Some underlying records still store Arabic content (e.g., `name_ar` on areas, developers, projects, currencies, translations). These are *data values*, not UI chrome. The admin must still be able to view/manage such data, but the surrounding UI is English LTR. Displaying an Arabic data value does not require flipping the page direction.

**Translations management screens**: Admin screens that exist to manage multi-locale *content/translations data* (e.g., a translations table) continue to display the stored locale values as data, while the management UI itself is English LTR.
**Mobile app unaffected**: Any shared i18n packages must keep serving Arabic to the mobile app; narrowing applies only to the admin dashboard's consumption.
**Missing English translation key**: Rendering must degrade gracefully (visible/detectable missing-key indicator), not crash or leave blank chrome.
**Browser/system set to Arabic locale**: The admin dashboard ignores it and serves English LTR.
functionalRequirements: **FR-001**: The admin dashboard MUST present a single user-facing locale (English) across all admin, engine, and product console screens.
**FR-002**: The admin dashboard MUST render with a single layout direction (LTR) for all chrome and layout; no screen may force or toggle RTL for the UI itself.
**FR-003**: The admin dashboard MUST remove all user-facing language-switching controls (no AR/EN toggle).

**FR-004**: All user-visible admin strings MUST resolve through the i18n mechanism using translation keys; hardcoded user-facing string literals are not permitted (this rule is unchanged from today, but now applies with English as the only catalog).
**FR-005**: The admin dashboard MUST load and ship only the English translation catalog; the Arabic catalog MUST NOT be loaded or required for admin rendering.
**FR-006**: Requests to previously valid Arabic/RTL admin URLs MUST resolve to the English LTR experience (redirect or transparent serve) without producing an error or broken layout.

**FR-007**: The admin dashboard MUST continue to display and manage records that contain locale-specific data values (e.g., Arabic name fields, translation entries) as *data*, without requiring the surrounding UI to switch direction or locale.
**FR-008**: A missing English translation key MUST degrade gracefully and detectably (developer-visible indicator), without breaking page layout or crashing the page.
**FR-009**: The change MUST NOT alter the mobile app's bilingual (AR/EN) or bidirectional (RTL/LTR) behavior; mobile remains out of scope and unaffected.

**FR-010**: The project constitution MUST be updated to state, as explicit and minimal rules, that admin dashboard pages are English-only, LTR-only, and route all strings through the English i18n catalog — with a short enumerable checklist for building any new admin page.
**FR-011**: The constitution rules MUST be expressed minimally enough that a developer can build a compliant new admin page from that section alone, without consulting other specs.

**FR-012**: Existing admin pages MUST be brought into compliance: removal of `dir="rtl"`/direction-aware UI styling on chrome, removal of Arabic UI strings/switchers, and confirmation that strings resolve from the English catalog.

assumptions: **Reuse of existing backend resources (hybrid delivery)**: selectable values are served through a consistent option shape by reusing existing resource list endpoints where the resource exists, and by adding lightweight dedicated option endpoints only for value sets with no list resource — per the user's intent to "use api resources for fetch values" (see Clarifications). Where a given value set has no backend source and is a purely fixed domain constant, it may remain a static list and is out of scope for conversion.
**Scope is the admin console**: this feature applies to the admin CRUD pages and their forms/filters. The mobile app is out of scope.
**Authorization and tenant scoping already exist** on the underlying resources and are reused; option sources do not introduce a new permission model, only respect the existing one.

**Single-language admin**: the admin console is English-only/LTR; "human-readable label" means the English/display label, while underlying data values (including any Arabic data) remain the stored values.
**Control look-and-feel** follows the established admin design system (consistent with other inputs), supporting light and dark themes and responsive widths from small to large screens.

**Existing patterns extend rather than replace**: the current async reference picker and static select are treated as the starting point to be unified/extended into the reusable approach, not thrown away — including fixing the known gap where a preselected reference value does not show its label on edit.
**Short-window caching** of option results is acceptable for freshness; near-real-time propagation of backend changes within an open form is not required.
edgeCases: **Large option sets**: a source with thousands of values must remain usable — the control searches/pages rather than loading everything at once, and remains responsive.
**No results**: when a search matches nothing, the control shows a clear empty state, not a spinner or an error.
**Slow or failed loads**: while options load the control shows a loading state; if loading fails it shows a retry-able error and does not silently appear empty.
**Stale/preselected value**: an existing stored value that no longer exists (deleted related record, retired code) is still shown as the current selection and visibly flagged rather than dropped.
**Permission / tenant scope**: options only include records the current operator is allowed to see; option lists respect the same tenant scoping and authorization as the underlying data.
**Duplicate labels**: two records with identical display labels are still distinguishable enough to select the intended one.
**Required vs optional**: required fields cannot be submitted empty; optional fields can be cleared.
**Rapid typing**: fast successive keystrokes do not produce out-of-order results or flicker; the latest query wins.
**Keyboard & assistive tech**: the control is fully operable by keyboard and announced correctly to screen readers.
functionalRequirements: **FR-001**: The admin MUST provide a reusable way to render a single-select dropdown whose options are supplied by the backend rather than hard-coded in the front end.
**FR-002**: The admin MUST provide a reusable type-ahead (autocomplete) variant of the same control for sources where the operator narrows results by typing a query.

**FR-003**: The reusable approach MUST NOT preclude a future multi-select variant backed by the same option source, but an API-backed multi-select control is NOT in this feature's MVP (deferred — see Out of Scope); all fields converted in this feature are single-value.
**FR-004**: Each option MUST present a human-readable label to the operator while the form stores the option's underlying value (identifier or code) for submission.

**FR-005**: A field MUST be declarable by configuration that names its option source, the control variant to use (MVP variants: `select` = load all options, `autocomplete` = server-searched type-ahead), and how each option's value and label are derived — with no per-field bespoke control required and no automatic select-vs-autocomplete size threshold.
**FR-006**: The same option source MUST be reusable across multiple forms and across list filters without duplicating its definition.

**FR-007**: When editing an existing record, each API-backed field MUST display the current selection's human-readable label on load, including resolving the label for a value that is not in the first page of results.
**FR-008**: The control MUST present distinct loading, empty (no matches), and error states; an error state MUST be recoverable (retry) and MUST NOT be presented as an empty list.
**FR-009**: For large option sets, the control MUST retrieve options incrementally (search and/or paging) rather than loading the entire set at once.
**FR-010**: Option data MUST respect the requesting operator's authorization and tenant scope, returning only values the operator is permitted to see.
**FR-011**: The system MUST prevent submission of a value that is not part of the field's allowed set, surfacing a clear validation message (client-side guidance plus server-side enforcement).
**FR-012**: A stored value that is no longer in the option source MUST remain visible as the current selection and be visibly flagged, rather than silently cleared or hidden.

**FR-013**: All operator-visible text in these controls (labels, placeholders, loading/empty/error messages) MUST come from the translation catalog, with no hard-coded strings, and MUST render correctly in both light and dark themes.
**FR-014**: The controls MUST be fully keyboard-operable and expose appropriate roles/labels for assistive technologies.

**FR-015**: The backend MUST expose selectable values for each source in a consistent, predictable shape (value plus label, optionally extra display metadata) so that any front-end control can consume any source uniformly. Sources MUST be served by a hybrid approach: reuse an existing resource's list endpoint (honoring `q`/paging) where that resource exists; provide a lightweight dedicated option endpoint only for value sets that have no list resource (e.g., currencies, countries, plans).

**FR-016**: Option results SHOULD be cached/deduplicated for a short window so repeated opens and identical queries do not refetch unnecessarily, while still reflecting backend changes on a subsequent open.

**FR-017**: All CRUD form fields across the admin that currently use a free-text input for a foreign-key identifier or a coded enumeration, and existing dropdowns whose options are hard-coded in the front end, MUST be converted to the API-backed control where a backend source for those values exists.
**FR-018**: Selecting, clearing, searching, and submitting MUST behave consistently across every instance of the control regardless of which source it is bound to.
