assumptions: The existing Kernel Notifications module provides (or can be extended to provide) a dispatcher, provider adapter, delivery-attempt records, queueing, dedup, and preference enforcement; this feature extends it rather than building anew. The audit (`research.md`) confirms exact capabilities before design.
The existing Kernel Settings module provides scoped settings, secret masking, and (likely) optimistic concurrency; audience URL + provider settings are added as new keys under existing conventions.
The active product is resolvable server-side from request context (host/header/route) per current OAR Engine conventions; client recovery binds to the resolved product.
User language/preferred locale is stored and readable per existing user-language implementation; AR and EN are the in-scope locales for OAR B (AR default).
The standard `password_reset_tokens` table and current real-broker behavior are retained; any extension for audience/product binding is additive and broker-compatible.
"Suspended"/"ineligible" account states are determined by existing account/eligibility rules in Identity; this feature reuses them for the generic-response rule rather than defining new states.
Admin recovery routes follow existing admin auth-route conventions; if a compatible public admin recovery route already exists it is repaired in place rather than duplicated.
edgeCases: An account that exists on both surfaces requests recovery via one route — only that route's audience/template/destination is used; a token issued for one audience/product cannot be silently redeemed in another.
A reset destination cannot be resolved (no setting, no env fallback) — fail closed, record a configuration error, send nothing.
A required transactional template has no published variant in any locale — configuration failure, never fall back to hardcoded Laravel copy.

A provider outage or auth failure during send — safe stable error returned, correlation ID retained for operators, no credential or account-existence leak; failed delivery does not reveal whether the email exists.
Concurrent settings edits — optimistic version conflict surfaced.
A published template is edited — prior published versions remain immutable; in-flight/historical delivery records keep their original template key + version.
Token replayed after a successful reset — rejected (single-use); expired or invalid token — rejected with stable codes.
Preview/test-send must never issue a real reset token or send to anyone other than the explicit test recipient.
Throttling thresholds exceeded — generic throttled response that still does not disclose account existence.
functionalRequirements: *Audience-aware URL resolution (US1)**
**FR-001**: System MUST select the recovery audience (admin vs client) solely from the route used, never from the request body.

**FR-002**: System MUST resolve all reset destinations server-side and validate them against configured trusted origins; the request MUST NOT be able to supply or override redirect URL, reset origin, template key, audience, product, or sender.

**FR-003**: System MUST use the configured admin reset URL for admin recovery and the active product's client reset URL or approved mobile universal/deep link for client recovery, with no cross-audience fallback.
**FR-004**: System MUST require HTTPS for reset URLs in non-local environments, permitting HTTP only for explicitly allowed local-development URLs.
**FR-005**: System MUST fail closed (record a configuration error, send nothing) when no valid reset destination can be resolved.
**FR-006**: System MUST generate reset link query parameters with proper URL encoding, include only the minimum required values, and never log tokens.

**FR-007**: Every `password_reset_request` MUST bind at minimum: user, normalized email, product, audience, broker-token reference / secure token correlation, expiration, consumed timestamp, and the request metadata needed for throttling + auditing. A token issued for one product or audience MUST be **rejected** when redeemed through another product or audience.
*Public client recovery (US2)**

**FR-008**: System MUST provide public, unauthenticated client forgot-password and reset-password endpoints (audited first; equivalent existing endpoints repaired in place, otherwise canonical endpoints equivalent to `POST /api/v1/auth/forgot-password` and `POST /api/v1/auth/reset-password`); duplicate routes are forbidden.

**FR-009**: Forgot-password MUST accept a normalized email, resolve the active product + client audience server-side via the extended `ProductContext` resolution (see FR-009a), and always return the same generic accepted response for existing, nonexistent, ineligible, suspended, and admin-only accounts (no existence disclosure).

**FR-009a**: Server-side product-context resolution (realized by **extending the existing `ProductContext`** service + `ProductClientCredentialService`, not a parallel resolver) MUST resolve product context in this order: (1) trusted request host/domain mapping (web clients), (2) validated product-scoped client credential (mobile/external clients, via the existing client-credential/settings architecture), (3) deployment-configured active product (single-product API), (4) **fail closed** when none resolves. A request-body `product_id` MUST NOT independently establish context; it is accepted only as a routing hint that matches the trusted host, client credential, or configured product. Admin recovery resolves the administration deployment/product context + `admin` audience; client recovery resolves the active end-user product + `client` audience.

**FR-010**: Forgot-password MUST throttle requests with these defaults (server/env-configurable, not Admin-UI-editable): reset-token lifetime **60 minutes**; minimum resend interval **60 seconds** per (normalized email, resolved product, resolved audience); **5 requests per 15 minutes** on the combined key (request IP + normalized-email hash + resolved product + resolved audience); plus a broad **IP-level limiter** against distributed enumeration/flooding. It MUST queue the email where the notification architecture supports queueing. HTTP **429** MAY be returned **only** for broad request/IP rate limiting and MUST NOT reveal account existence (account-specific throttling still returns the generic accepted response).
**FR-011**: Reset-password MUST accept email, token, password, and confirmation, and MUST validate token expiry, audience, product context, and single-use status before applying the new password.

**FR-012**: On successful reset, the system MUST consume/revoke the token and invalidate **all** authentication state for the user: delete/revoke all Sanctum personal access tokens, invalidate all server-side web sessions, rotate `remember_token`, invalidate refresh tokens/equivalents, and clear any still-usable password-reset requests for that user. The flow MUST NOT preserve or auto-authenticate the current device. The system MUST publish and audit a **password-reset-completed** security event containing identifiers + correlation metadata only — never passwords, raw reset tokens, reset URLs, or session credentials.
**FR-013**: Reset-password MUST return stable machine-readable error codes via the normalized API error envelope without exposing sensitive details.

**FR-014**: The end-user client MUST provide (or integrate) a forgot-password request flow with a generic success state, a reset-password screen reachable from the approved link/deep link, AR and EN messages, and correct handling of expired, invalid, and already-used tokens.
*Administrator recovery (US3)**

**FR-015**: System MUST provide admin forgot-password and reset-password recovery (audited first; existing compatible public/documented route preserved, otherwise admin-audience endpoints equivalent to `POST /api/v1/admin/auth/forgot-password` and `POST /api/v1/admin/auth/reset-password`).

**FR-016**: Admin recovery endpoints MUST be unauthenticated (pre-login) yet issue admin-audience recovery only for eligible platform/admin accounts, returning the same generic accepted response for nonexistent/ineligible accounts.
**FR-017**: Admin recovery links MUST always resolve to the admin reset page and MUST NOT silently fall back to a client URL.
**FR-018**: Admin and client routes MAY reuse the same Identity actions, but audience selection MUST be explicit and server-controlled per route.
*Mail-provider settings (US4)**

**FR-019**: System MUST support scoped mail-provider settings covering at minimum: provider/driver, SMTP host/port, encryption mode, SMTP username, SMTP password/credential, sender email, sender display name, reply-to email + name, connection timeout (where supported), queue selection (where supported), provider enabled/disabled state, admin frontend/reset URL, client frontend/reset URL, optional client universal/deep-link reset URL, and support email.

**FR-020**: System MUST store secrets through the existing protected settings/secret mechanism as write-only/masked, and MUST never expose stored secrets in API responses, audit snapshots, logs, validation errors, or UI.

**FR-021**: System MUST support platform defaults and product-scoped overrides, and MUST resolve values by deterministic precedence: product-scoped validated → platform-scoped validated → environment fallback (`ADMIN_FRONTEND_URL`, `CLIENT_FRONTEND_URL`, optional approved mobile/universal link) → explicit configuration failure.
**FR-022**: System MUST provide an authorized test-connection/test-email operation and record its result (and provider failures) without exposing credentials.

**FR-023**: System MUST audit every successful settings mutation with actor, scope, product, changed keys, and correlation ID, and MUST use optimistic version/conflict handling where Kernel Settings already supports it.

**FR-024**: System MUST expose audience-aware URL settings (semantic equivalents of `identity.admin_frontend_url`, `identity.admin_reset_password_url`, `identity.client_frontend_url`, `identity.client_reset_password_url`, optional `identity.client_reset_deep_link`, `identity.support_email`), replacing the ambiguous single `frontend_url` concept; exact keys MAY follow existing settings naming conventions.
*Template management (US5)**

**FR-025**: System MUST provide a versioned email-template catalog owned by `kernel.notifications`, seeded idempotently in AR and EN for at least `identity.password_reset`, `identity.welcome`, `notifications.generic`, and `marketing.offer`, extensible to new message types without schema changes or new hardcoded template columns.

**FR-026**: Each template MUST capture: stable template key, internal name, audience (`admin`/`client`/`shared`), category (`transactional`/`operational`/`marketing`), scope (platform default or product override), locale, subject, HTML body, plain-text body, declared variable schema, lifecycle state (draft/published/archived), version number, author, created/updated/published timestamps, and optional preview/sample values.

**FR-027**: System MUST support template create, edit, duplicate, preview, test-send, publish, and archive; editing a published template MUST create a new draft version while previously published versions remain immutable.
**FR-028**: System MUST resolve exactly one active published version per (scope, message type, audience, locale) tuple.

**FR-029**: System MUST block publishing a system template unless required AR and EN variants exist for products supporting both locales, and MUST reject publishing a template with unknown, missing, or unsafe variables.

**FR-030**: System MUST prevent archived templates from being selected for new delivery and MUST retain the template key + immutable version on existing delivery records (soft archive, never destructive deletion of published history).
*Variables & safe rendering (US6)**

**FR-031**: System MUST validate bound variables against the template's declared schema before dispatch, escape HTML-interpolated values by default, validate URLs before rendering, and generate + verify both HTML and plain-text output.
**FR-032**: System MUST prevent unauthenticated callers from supplying system-controlled variables (`reset_url`, recipient email, product identity, expiry).
**FR-033**: System MUST reject template content containing raw executable code, scripts, arbitrary PHP, Blade directives, remote includes, or unsafe HTML.

**FR-034**: Preview MUST use clearly marked sample data and never generate a real reset token; test-send MUST use the production renderer + provider adapter and send only to an explicitly entered authorized test recipient.
*Locale-aware delivery (US7)**
**FR-035**: System MUST resolve delivery locale in order: stored user locale → validated locale on a trusted notification request → active product default locale → platform default locale.
**FR-036**: System MUST render AR HTML with `lang="ar"` + RTL and EN HTML with `lang="en"` + LTR.

**FR-037**: System MUST follow a documented locale fallback chain when a preferred-locale variant is missing and record the fallback used; missing all published variants for a required transactional message MUST be treated as a configuration failure (never hardcoded Laravel copy).
*Welcome / operational / promotional reuse (US8)**

**FR-038**: Successful end-user registration MUST request the configured `identity.welcome` message through the existing notification dispatcher; admin registration/invitation MAY use an admin-specific welcome/invitation binding.

**FR-039**: Existing operational notifications and offer/promotional sends MUST select a published template where applicable, reusing the existing notification system without building a second notification system or a marketing-automation/CRM/segmentation platform.

**FR-040**: Where no campaign-targeting system exists, marketing scope MUST be limited to template management, preview/test-send, explicit/existing-recipient workflows, and a **reusable dispatch contract** for future callers (defined in `contracts/notification-dispatch-contract.md`). The reusable dispatch contract is a small application/kernel contract accepting at minimum: product context; optional organization context; recipient or recipient reference; template key/version; locale; channel set; validated template variables; audience/deep-link URLs where applicable; deduplication/idempotency key; optional scheduling timestamp; correlation identifier; and the requesting actor or system source. It MUST return/expose a stable dispatch/request identifier and MUST let later callers dispatch without knowing SMTP/provider internals. Explicitly **out of scope** (resolving A1, no campaign-management platform): campaign authoring, audience segmentation, marketing journeys, campaign analytics, bulk campaign scheduling UI, and mailing-list management.

**FR-041**: `marketing.offer` messages MUST dispatch **only** when the recipient has active, verifiable marketing consent/preference for the channel; if the audit finds no authoritative consent source, promotional dispatch is **disabled by default** (the feature may add the minimum consent/preference record or integrate a planned privacy-consent system, but MUST NOT infer consent from registration alone). Every marketing email MUST include a **signed, unauthenticated, idempotent unsubscribe link** that exposes only minimal recipient/product/preference context (no unnecessary raw user id), updates the existing marketing preference/consent source, and records the change + correlation metadata. Unsubscribe/opt-out MUST NOT suppress password-reset, security, or legally/operationally necessary transactional messages. Operational notifications MUST honor their applicable preferences; transactional password-reset delivery MUST remain available independently of marketing opt-out.
*Admin API & permissions**

**FR-042**: System MUST provide platform mail-settings operations (read effective settings, update allowed settings, test connection/test email, masked-secrets-only responses) and platform template operations (list/filter, read with versions + localized variants, create draft, update draft, duplicate, preview, test-send, publish, archive, view delivery/reference history where available).

**FR-043**: System MUST provide product-scoped template + binding operations under the current admin product-routing convention (e.g. `/api/v1/admin/products/{product}/email-templates` and `/email-template-bindings`) and MUST derive product context from the route/active context, never trusting a body-supplied product identifier.

**FR-044**: System MUST declare granular permissions and enforce authorization on every state-changing admin operation plus write an audit record for each. The permission ownership boundary is explicit (resolving U1):
**`kernel.notifications.email_settings.view`/`.update`** — owned by `kernel.notifications`; controls SMTP / email-delivery provider settings only.
**`kernel.notifications.email_templates.view`/`.create`/`.update`/`.publish`/`.archive`/`.test_send`** — owned by `kernel.notifications`; controls the email-template catalog and editor operations.

**`kernel.settings.audience_urls.view`/`.update`** — owned and declared by **`kernel.settings`** (NOT notifications); controls audience destination URL settings (e.g. identity verification, password-reset, invitation, unsubscribe, admin/client frontend + reset URLs). These are authorized independently from `email_settings.*`: holding one MUST NOT grant the other.
*Admin UI**

**FR-045**: System MUST provide Engine Console screens for mail provider/settings (masked credentials, sender identity, admin + default client URL config, test-email) and a platform template catalog with editor, AR/EN tabs, HTML + text preview (AR RTL / EN LTR), variable reference panel, version history, publish/archive controls, and binding status/validation errors.

**FR-046**: System MUST provide Product Console screens for product URL overrides (where allowed), product template overrides, product message-type bindings, product branding preview, locale-completeness status, and product-context test-send.

**FR-047**: Admin UI MUST remain English-only/LTR-only, MUST never display a stored SMTP secret after saving, MUST NOT add end-user account-recovery screens, and MUST use the Admin Resource Framework only where appropriate (the template editor/preview/publish/test-send/version-history remains a specialized workflow), built with the `shadcn` skill in light + dark mode and responsive.
*Security & privacy**
**FR-048**: Forgot-password responses MUST NOT allow account enumeration; the system MUST apply request throttling plus Laravel broker throttling.
**FR-049**: Reset tokens MUST be cryptographically secure, hashed at rest where supported, expiring, and single-use.
**FR-050**: Reset URLs, tokens, passwords, SMTP credentials, and rendered sensitive values MUST NOT appear in logs or audit snapshots, and password values MUST NEVER be included in events.
**FR-051**: Template HTML MUST be sanitized; test-send MUST require explicit permission and be audited.

**FR-052**: Provider failures MUST return safe stable errors and retain correlation IDs for operators; public endpoints MUST use the normalized API error envelope; new stable error codes are append-only; client behavior MUST NOT branch on translated error messages.
*Data, persistence & compatibility**

**FR-053**: System MUST audit existing tables before adding any; the target model MAY introduce semantic equivalents of `email_templates`, `email_template_versions`, and `email_template_bindings`, and MUST reuse existing notification-request and delivery-attempt tables rather than duplicating them.

**FR-054**: System MUST audit whether the standard `password_reset_tokens` structure is sufficient and, if insufficient, extend it compatibly or introduce an owned reset-request record — without removing the standard table or breaking Laravel broker compatibility absent documented justification + migration evidence.

**FR-055**: Migrations MUST follow expand → seed/backfill → switch reads → enforce; existing hardcoded password-reset/welcome content MUST remain available as controlled compatibility defaults during rollout and stop being the primary runtime source once published templates are verified.

**FR-056**: System MUST preserve: the recently added `password_reset_tokens` migration, the working real-broker behavior, existing compatible `/api/v1` routes, and MUST NOT restore reliance on Laravel's nonexistent `password.reset` web route, create parallel mail/template/notification/translation/audit systems, store secrets in Product Manifests, or introduce domain-specific concepts into Kernel Identity/Notifications/Settings.
*Documentation & contracts**

**FR-057**: For every new or changed endpoint, the team MUST update `docs/api-endpoints.md`, add/update `packages/api-tests/` coverage, and regenerate + commit OpenAPI TypeScript types when the contract changes.

**FR-058**: The team MUST update `.env.example` (separated admin/client URL fallbacks), the settings catalog + ownership metadata, module manifests (permissions, settings, tables, events), mail/template operator docs, product setup docs, a deployment checklist (required production URLs, HTTPS constraints, provider credentials, sender verification, test-send verification), the error-code catalog (if new codes), and the event catalog (if new versioned Identity/Notification events), and MUST document the URL- and locale-resolution algorithms explicitly.

*Independent Test**: Trigger admin and client forgot-password through their respective routes and assert (via the notification fake) that the rendered link uses the configured admin reset URL vs the active product's client reset URL/deep link respectively, that no body field changes the destination, and that an unresolvable destination fails closed.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:

*Why this priority**: The client is the primary audience and the surface that was broken in production. Recovery must actually complete (token issued → email → reset → login) for the feature to deliver value.

*Independent Test**: From the client repository layer, call the public forgot-password endpoint for existing, nonexistent, ineligible, and suspended emails and assert identical generic responses; then complete a reset with a real issued token and assert login works, single-use enforcement, and expiry/invalid handling — all without mocking the broker.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: Admin recovery must be isolated from client recovery for both correctness and security; it shares Identity actions but requires explicit, server-controlled audience selection.

*Independent Test**: Call the admin forgot-password route for an eligible admin and a non-admin and assert identical generic responses, that the link resolves to the admin reset page, and that audience is server-selected (never body-driven). Reuse of Identity actions is verified without leaking the client destination.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:

*Why this priority**: Reliable delivery and operator self-service depend on scoped, secure settings; required before templates can be exercised against a real provider, but recovery can ship on env fallback first.

*Independent Test**: Update non-secret settings via the platform settings API and read them back masked; store a secret and confirm it is never returned/logged/audited in clear; run test-send and confirm a recorded result without credential exposure; verify resolution precedence (product → platform → env → failure).
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: Templates remove hardcoded copy and enable localization/branding; required for AR/EN reset & welcome emails, but recovery wiring (P1) can resolve a seeded default first.

*Independent Test**: Run the draft→publish→archive lifecycle; confirm editing a published template creates a new draft while prior published versions stay immutable; confirm exactly one active published version resolves per (scope, message type, audience, locale); confirm publish is blocked when required AR/EN variants are missing for dual-locale products; confirm archived templates are not selectable for new delivery.
*Acceptance Scenarios**:
*Why this priority**: Safe rendering is a security boundary (escaping, no executable code, no client-supplied `reset_url`) and a correctness guarantee for variable schemas.

*Independent Test**: Render password-reset and welcome templates with their declared variables and assert HTML+text output and escaping; attempt to inject scripts/PHP/Blade/remote includes/unsafe HTML and assert rejection; attempt to supply `reset_url`/recipient/product/expiry from an unauthenticated request and assert it is ignored; run preview and assert sample data and no real token.

*Independent Test**: Set a user's stored locale to AR then EN and assert the corresponding subject/HTML/text; assert AR renders `lang="ar"` + RTL and EN renders `lang="en"` + LTR; remove the preferred-locale variant and assert the documented fallback is used and recorded; remove all published variants for a required transactional message and assert a configuration failure (not hardcoded Laravel copy).

*Why this priority**: Demonstrates the shared pipeline's reach and removes more hardcoded copy, but depends on P1/P2 being in place and is the least urgent slice.

*Independent Test**: Register an end user and assert the configured `identity.welcome` message is requested through the existing dispatcher; send an operational notification and a marketing offer and assert each selects a published template, honors applicable preferences/marketing consent, and that password-reset delivery is unaffected by marketing opt-out.

assumptions: **Generalization of Feature 065** *(decided — see Clarifications 2026-07-02)*: This spec lifts the message-type → binding → template mechanism proven in Feature 065 (email delivery + mail recovery) into a **channel-agnostic routing capability**. The chosen approach is to **extract** the routing/resolution logic into a channel-agnostic layer that the existing email path **consumes**, **reusing 065's existing data model and services** — no forked or duplicate template/binding subsystem is created (consistent with 065's own "do not create a second template subsystem" rule and the constitution's DRY / single-source-of-truth principle). No new delivery channel is wired in this feature; email remains the sole consumer, now sitting on top of the extracted layer.

**Single wired channel for now**: Adding new delivery channels (push, SMS, in-app as *managed-template* consumers) is **out of scope**; this feature defines and hardens the routing/binding contract, not new transports.

**Existing authoring surfaces reused**: Template and binding authoring already exist in the Engine Console (platform scope) and Product Console (product scope). This feature does not re-specify those UIs; it specifies the routing/resolution capability they feed.
**Audience derivation exists**: The recipient's audience (internal-admin vs end-client) is derivable from identity/authorization without caller input.
**Trusted context sources exist**: Product context and the locale candidate chain are obtainable from trusted server-side context (active product/route, recipient profile, product/platform defaults).

**Rendering is a downstream concern**: Variable substitution and channel-specific formatting belong to the consumer that renders a resolved template; this spec requires that variables are populated and that unmet variables never leak template syntax, but does not redefine the rendering engine.

**"Required-transactional" is a system-owned property** *(decided — see Clarifications 2026-07-02)*: it is declared in a code+config registry of message types (e.g. account recovery), not an administrator-toggleable field, so fail-closed behavior cannot be disabled through the admin UI. The resolver and the readiness check read this one registry.
edgeCases: **No active binding for the tuple** → the message type is treated as non-managed for that context; required-transactional types fail closed, others degrade gracefully (never fabricated content for a required transactional).
**Bound template later archived/unpublished** → the binding stops resolving (published-only rule) exactly as if it pointed nowhere; behavior is identical to "no match."

**Two bindings attempt to be active for one tuple** (including two administrators activating simultaneously) → the dual-layer one-active-per-tuple invariant must prevent it; the database partial-unique index rejects the second concurrent activation and the application layer performs an atomic activate/deactivate (activating one deactivates the prior).
**Recipient audience is ambiguous or shared** → exact-audience binding wins; if only a `shared` binding exists it is used; if both exist, exact wins.
**Preferred locale has no published variant but another locale does** → deliver the available published variant and record that a fallback occurred.
**Required transactional with zero published variants anywhere** → fail closed and surface; do not deliver.

**Producer emits context missing a variable the template expects** → surfaced by a pre-runtime readiness/variable-contract check; at delivery, unmet variables must not leak template syntax to the recipient.
**Product context is absent** → only platform-scope bindings are considered.
**Message type resolves to a template whose scope/product does not match the request** → concealed as "no match" (a cross-scope/cross-product template is never disclosed via routing).

**Binding changes after a message is queued but before it is delivered** → because resolution is late-binding (at delivery), the queued/scheduled send uses the binding active at delivery time, not the one active when the event was raised; the delivery record captures the version actually used.
functionalRequirements: **FR-001**: Producers MUST request a notification by a stable, human-meaningful **message-type identifier** plus recipient and context data — never by a direct template identifier.
**FR-002**: The system MUST maintain administrator-managed **bindings**, each mapping a routing tuple *(message type, audience, scope, product, locale)* to exactly one target template.

**FR-003**: The system MUST enforce **at most one active binding per routing tuple** at any time; activating a binding MUST atomically supersede any previously active binding for that tuple. Enforcement MUST be **dual-layer** (defense-in-depth per the constitution): a **database partial-unique constraint/index** guaranteeing one active binding per tuple even under concurrent writes, PLUS an **application-layer atomic activate/deactivate** for correct, friendly behavior. The invariant MUST hold when two administrators activate competing bindings for the same tuple simultaneously.
**FR-004**: At delivery time, the system MUST resolve the target template from the active binding matching the request's message type, resolved audience, applicable scope/product, and chosen locale.
**FR-005**: Resolution MUST prefer a **product-scoped** active binding over a **platform-scoped** binding whenever a trusted product context is present, and fall back to platform scope otherwise.
**FR-006**: Resolution MUST prefer an **exact audience** match over a **shared** (any-audience) binding for the same tuple.
**FR-007**: Only a **published** template version is eligible for resolution; a binding pointing to a draft, unpublished, or archived template MUST be treated as "no match."

**FR-008**: Administrators MUST be able to re-target a message type to a different published template **solely by changing bindings**, with the change taking effect **without any code change or redeployment**. Resolution is **late-binding** (FR-004): the template is resolved at delivery time, so the change applies to every not-yet-delivered message — including already-queued and scheduled/future-dated sends. No template snapshot is captured on the request when the event is raised; the actual version used is recorded on the delivery (FR-015).

**FR-009**: The system MUST resolve delivery locale via an ordered candidate chain — recipient's stored locale → trusted request locale → product default → platform default — and, if the preferred locale has no published variant, fall back to any published variant of the same tuple, recording that a fallback occurred.

**FR-010**: For message types designated **required-transactional**, if no published variant exists in **any** locale, the system MUST **fail closed** — it MUST NOT deliver fabricated or hardcoded content — and MUST surface the unmet requirement.

**FR-010a**: The set of required-transactional message types MUST be defined in a **system-owned registry** (code + configuration), NOT as an administrator-toggleable data attribute — the fail-closed property cannot be disabled through the admin surface. This registry is the single authoritative source consulted by both the resolver (FR-010) and the readiness check (FR-021).
**FR-011**: For **non-required** message types with no resolvable managed template, the system MAY degrade gracefully to a minimal fallback rather than failing the request.

**FR-012**: The product context used for scope resolution MUST derive from **trusted server-side context** (route/active context), and MUST NOT be taken from a recipient- or request-body-supplied product identifier.
**FR-013**: The recipient's **audience** (e.g. internal-admin vs end-client) MUST be derived from the recipient's own identity/authorization, not supplied by the caller.

**FR-014**: Producer-supplied context data MUST populate the resolved template's declared **variables**; the expected variable set per message type SHOULD be declarable and verifiable independently of a live send.
**FR-015**: The system MUST record, for each managed delivery, **which template and template version** were resolved and used, for audit, observability, and troubleshooting.

**FR-016**: Administrators MUST be able to author templates and bindings at **two scopes** — platform (defaults for all products) and product (per-product overrides) — with product overriding platform per FR-005.
**FR-017**: Binding and template management actions MUST be **authorization-gated**, and administrative changes to bindings/templates MUST be **audited**.
**FR-018**: A single message type MAY serve more than one audience via a **shared** binding; the resolver MUST apply the audience precedence in FR-006 deterministically.
**FR-019**: Introducing a new message type MUST NOT require changes to the resolution engine — only a new producer emit, a published template, and an active binding.

**FR-020**: When multiple candidate bindings could match, precedence order — scope (product before platform), then audience (exact before shared), then locale chain — MUST fully and deterministically select a single winner.

**FR-021**: The system MUST provide a **pre-runtime readiness check**, delivered as a **CLI/ops command runnable against a live environment**, that — for each message type listed in the required-transactional registry (FR-010a) — verifies a resolvable published template and a satisfied variable contract for every required audience/scope, so gaps are caught before they affect real deliveries. It generalizes 065's existing recovery-only readiness command to the full registry. A build-time CI gate is explicitly NOT used, because published-template state is per-environment database data that a build pipeline cannot truthfully evaluate.
**FR-022**: Routing MUST NOT disclose the existence of a cross-scope or cross-product template it is not entitled to use for the current request; such cases MUST be indistinguishable from "no match."

functionalRequirements: **FR-001**: The supported queue/Horizon service MUST start and remain in a healthy, non-crash-looping state throughout a continuous 10-minute verification window.
**FR-002**: The application and worker runtimes MUST resolve a compatible set of installed dependencies and registered service providers for their approved environment contexts.
**FR-003**: Development-only providers MUST NOT prevent worker or non-development runtime boot when those providers are not installed or authorized for that context.
**FR-004**: The worker MUST consume from the configured Redis queue connection unless a current authoritative repository contract establishes a different supported connection before planning.

**FR-005**: Worker configuration MUST NOT silently differ from the main application runtime in any setting that changes application boot, job serialization, encryption, queue routing, or provider behavior.
**FR-006**: Startup or connection failures MUST produce visible diagnostic output and a non-success health state that distinguishes starting, running, unhealthy, and crash-looping behavior.
**FR-007**: Restarting only the worker service MUST restore healthy processing without requiring unrelated services to be rebuilt or restarted when their state is already valid.
**FR-008**: At least one representative generic queued job MUST be dispatched asynchronously, consumed by a live worker, and verified through its completed effect and terminal state.
**FR-009**: Work queued before worker startup or during worker unavailability MUST remain available for later processing and MUST NOT be silently abandoned.
**FR-010**: Existing idempotency and duplicate-execution protections MUST remain intact; restart testing MUST detect unexplained duplicate side effects.

**FR-011**: At least one existing queued reset-password or equivalent email workflow MUST be triggered through its real entry path and MUST reach Mailpit within 60 seconds under the supported verification environment.
**FR-012**: Queue-backed email verification MUST assert worker consumption and the delivered external effect, not merely successful dispatch.
**FR-013**: No mail, notification, broadcast, or job workflow MAY be changed to synchronous execution solely to conceal worker failure or make verification pass.

**FR-014**: At least one deliberately failing test job MUST exercise configured attempt behavior and appear in the project's canonical failure mechanism with job identity, queue identity, attempts, timestamp, and actionable exception context.
**FR-015**: A documented retry or recovery procedure MUST be executed against controlled failed work and MUST produce an observable final outcome without silently deleting failure history.

**FR-016**: Temporary Redis unavailability MUST result in truthful degraded or unhealthy worker status, visible diagnostics, and preservation of pending work where the existing queue durability contract permits.
**FR-017**: Worker process termination followed by restart MUST be verified with pending or in-progress work and MUST not cause silent loss or unexplained duplicate effects.

**FR-018**: Queue verification MUST expose enough stable evidence for notification plumbing, early operational-health substrate, CI pipeline recovery, queue-backed contract verification, and provider/readiness checks without creating those downstream capabilities in this child.
**FR-019**: Existing public API behavior MUST remain unchanged unless a versioned change is explicitly approved under Program 069 FR-021; no endpoint may be added or changed merely to test the queue.
**FR-020**: Existing Dockerized runtime discipline, queue/Horizon ownership, kernel/domain/product boundaries, audit and correlation behavior, and secrets-management rules MUST be preserved.

**FR-021**: This child MUST NOT introduce notification types, reminder workflows, email templates, provider migrations, dashboards, health UI, client changes, admin pages, or other product capability.

**FR-022**: Backend regression coverage MUST include automatable worker boot/configuration behavior, successful and failed job behavior, asynchronous queued mail behavior, and relevant Pest coverage for every changed Laravel service, provider, job, or configuration rule.

**FR-023**: Black-box evidence MUST trigger an existing queue-backed workflow through its real entry path, observe its external effect through Mailpit or the canonical test provider, and confirm that the job drains or reaches its expected terminal state.

**FR-024**: Runtime evidence MUST include service/process status, successful boot logs, queue connection and visibility, successful processing, failed-work visibility, restart/recovery execution, and exact pass/fail/skip counts.

**FR-025**: Regression evidence MUST cover the relevant backend Pest suite, password-reset and notification API integration tests, queue-backed email behavior, container startup, and affected CI gate commands; any API-triggered workflow MUST retain its existing endpoint contract coverage.

**FR-026**: The child exit MUST follow Program 069 FR-018 and include the exact commit SHA, commands, environment and runtime/container names, ISO-8601 timestamps, true exit codes, exact pass/fail/skip counts, relevant service logs, queue/Horizon status, successful-job artifact, redacted Mailpit delivery artifact, failed-job/retry artifact, restart/recovery artifact, configuration-diff summary, executable rollback or forward-fix procedure, residual risks, audit-068 traceability, and explicit named approval.
**FR-027**: Evidence artifacts MUST exclude email content, credentials, tokens, personal data, secrets, private keys, and other prohibited sensitive material.

**FR-028**: Rollback planning MUST identify the application/worker configuration, dependency lockfiles, container images, volumes, and environment configuration that must move together; preserve pending and failed work where safely possible; detect recurrence of the original crash loop; and prefer a forward fix when rollback would restore non-processing queues.
**FR-029**: A destructive queue purge MUST NOT be the default rollback or recovery procedure, and failed or pending jobs MUST NOT be silently deleted.
**FR-030**: The child MAY transition to `VERIFIED` only after an FR-018-compliant committed evidence bundle is approved; its verification MUST NOT independently close P0 or produce a readiness state.

assumptions: Feature 088 is treated as the verified source of truth because `delivery-ledger.md` records it as Verified on 2026-07-09. Its contract document remains the console's binding dependency.
The console may call Feature 088's existing Admin API contract; the CLI-equivalent contract is evidence/support context, not a UI runtime path.

Feature 088's residual risks do not require new console telemetry. The console can represent request failures, bootstrap outages, timeout behavior, and unavailable dimensions truthfully as unavailable/unknown/error states.
The target users are platform operators using the existing Engine Console, not product admins or customers.
The operational-health page is an admin operational surface, so English-only LTR admin localization rules apply.
No backend change is expected for this child. Any backend touch discovered during planning is exceptional and requires explicit parity checks and dependency-regression analysis.
edgeCases: Feature 088 returns a dimension field as absent or malformed: the console MUST treat it as a contract error/unknown state, not healthy.
One dimension endpoint fails while others succeed: the failed dimension MUST render an error/unavailable state while successful dimensions remain visible.
All operational-health endpoints fail due to an application/bootstrap outage: the page MUST show the whole operational substrate as unavailable/unknown and MUST NOT present stale success.

Feature 088's known residual risks surface in practice: complete Redis outage or slow storage-outage response MUST be represented as unavailable/unknown/error in the console; this child MUST NOT add new probes to compensate.
Failed-job list is empty: the UI MUST show an explicit empty state distinct from unavailable or unknown.
Retry is double-clicked or the job disappears between list and action: the UI MUST display Feature 088's returned `not_found` or terminal outcome without inventing success.
Push provider is not configured: the UI MUST render `not_configured` as intentionally absent, not as failed, unknown, or healthy.
Operator permissions change during a session: after refresh or revalidation, navigation and actions MUST reflect the current permissions and backend 403 responses MUST be shown truthfully.
Mobile/narrow viewport: operational cards/tables/actions MUST remain readable and non-overlapping from approximately 375px through desktop.
functionalRequirements: *Feature 088 contract consumption**
**FR-001**: The console MUST consume only Feature 088's verified operational-health contract for worker, failed jobs, retry, scheduler, delivery trace, providers, storage, and data-layer health.

**FR-002**: The console MUST NOT introduce new telemetry, new backend probes, new health dimensions, new queue/provider/storage/database/cache inspection logic, or a second health contract. Any discovered inability to satisfy this spec from Feature 088's contract MUST be reported as a dependency regression and stop this child.

**FR-003**: The console MUST preserve Feature 088 state semantics exactly, including `healthy`, `degraded`, `unavailable`, `unknown`, `not_configured`, `running`, `stopped`, `fresh`, `stale`, `pending`, `sent`, `failed`, `skipped`, `propagated`, `missing`, and `mismatched` where those states apply.
**FR-004**: The console MUST never render failed, unavailable, absent, malformed, unauthorized, or timed-out data as empty, neutral, or healthy.
**FR-005**: The console MUST show every required health dimension in the page experience: worker, failed jobs, scheduler, delivery trace, providers, storage, database, cache, and correlation status.
*Engine Console experience**
**FR-006**: The Engine Console MUST include an operational-health page or page set reachable only inside the Engine Console area and not inside any Product Console or client app.

**FR-007**: The operational-health surface MUST present a scan-friendly overview of all required dimensions, with state, last checked/observed timestamps when supplied, and enough context to distinguish healthy, degraded, unavailable, unknown, and not configured states.

**FR-008**: Each dimension MUST provide loading, empty, non-empty, unavailable, unknown, and error states where applicable; an empty state is allowed only when the Feature 088 contract reports a successful empty result.
**FR-009**: The page MUST be responsive and readable in light and dark modes from approximately 375px viewport width through desktop, with no overlapping text, controls, tables, or status indicators.
**FR-010**: All visible text MUST use the admin English/LTR localization catalog; this internal admin surface MUST NOT add Arabic/RTL branching or client-facing localization work.
*Failed jobs and retry**
**FR-011**: The failed-jobs section MUST display Feature 088's paginated failed-job records, including stable identifier, queue, bounded exception summary, failure timestamp, and pagination metadata.

**FR-012**: The retry action MAY be present only because Feature 088 already supports `POST /admin/operational-health/failed-jobs/{uuid}/retry`; the console MUST NOT implement or simulate retry locally.

**FR-013**: Every retry attempt initiated from the console MUST display the exact returned outcome and audit reference, if supplied; `retry_unavailable`, `retry_unconfirmed`, `re_failed`, and `not_found` MUST be treated as first-class outcomes, not UI errors to hide.
*Permissions and audit visibility**

**FR-014**: The operational-health navigation entry and every page route MUST require Engine Console access plus `kernel.observability.view`; backend authorization failures MUST be surfaced truthfully.

**FR-015**: Retry controls MUST require `kernel.observability.manage` in the UI, in addition to the backend's authoritative permission check. Read permission alone MUST NOT expose retry controls as enabled.
**FR-016**: The UI MUST make clear when an action outcome is audit-backed by Feature 088 and MUST NOT claim an audit entry exists if the contract did not return one.
*Finding closure and evidence**

**FR-017**: This child MUST remove or close the relevant Engine Console operational-health missing-surface finding only after implementation evidence proves the real page exists, is reachable in navigation, consumes Feature 088, renders all required states, and passes required verification.
**FR-018**: The finding disposition update MUST cite this child's committed FR-018 evidence bundle, not this spec alone and not Feature 088's backend-only evidence alone.

**FR-019**: The implementation plan MUST include admin typecheck, lint, production build, light/dark responsive UI checks, page-inventory coverage, and focused admin E2E or equivalent route/action coverage for the new page(s).

**FR-020**: If implementation touches any backend contract, docs, generated API types, or runtime endpoint behavior, the plan MUST include API-contract/runtime parity checks and treat that backend touch as an exception requiring explicit justification; absent such a verified need, backend contracts remain untouched.

**FR-021**: The console MUST preserve kernel/domain boundaries: no Real Estate/domain imports, product-domain assumptions, tenant-specific business data, or Product Console logic may enter kernel/admin shell operational-health logic.
